About Black Forest Labs

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX — foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and videos. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.

Why This Role

Frontier image and video models are now good enough that the hard question is no longer whether they work, but whether a new one is actually better, and how you'd know. Aesthetics, prompt following, editing fidelity, text rendering, character consistency: none of these collapse into a single number, and public benchmarks have fallen well behind the models they're meant to measure.

You'll work on the system BFL uses to answer that question. Every FLUX checkpoint, every finetuning and RL run, and every competitor release goes through our evaluation stack, and you'll help build and sharpen it. Product Research relies on what it shows to decide what to fix next, and to confirm the fix worked.

It gets harder from here. FLUX 3 is our first multimodal model, spanning image, video, audio and action, and each new modality needs its own way of being measured.

What You'll Work On

What you focus on will depend on where you're strongest and what the team needs most when you join.

In scope:

  • Building and maintaining the evaluation stack that every model checkpoint has to pass through and prove itself on, from automated benchmarking and LLM-as-judge pipelines, to human evaluation through panels (Prolific and otherwise).

  • Designing the breadth of evaluation across the taxonomy, from prompt adherence, editing fidelity, aesthetics, text rendering, subject and character consistency, to safety.

  • Evaluating the evaluation stack itself: checking that human and automated evals agree, that results stay stable over time, and improving them when they don't.

  • Benchmarking FLUX against the frontier models continuously, while obtaining a meaningful perspective on where we are better or worse than competitors and what such differences really mean.

  • Finding the ways in which the quality of the model's output falls short that are not captured by aggregate numbers.

  • Closing the loop, ideally, with the RL and finetuning researchers, by defining target metrics for them to aim for, and verifying that a new checkpoint improved the weakness without introducing new ones.

  • Designing how best to exploit the signals we already capture through the API and MCP, and what new signals we should capture, with help from research, data engineering and legal.

  • Maintaining the usefulness of existing metrics as their natural lifecycle brings up concerns of gaming and overfitting, and anticipating this for new metrics.

What We're Looking For

You have made meaningful contributions to the evaluation of generative models already. You understand that a benchmark figure without careful consideration of sample size and judge agreement with humans is at best uninformed optimism and at worst dangerously misleading, and you have been the person that found that inconvenient regression that nobody wanted to talk about.

You likely have:

  • Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in a relevant field or demonstrated equivalent practical experience

  • Practical experience with evaluating generative models, in a hands-on way. You may have worked with diffusion or flow-matching based image or video models already, but the capability to evaluate them in earnest transfers to other modalities too

  • Very strong Python and software engineering skills, with pipelines that run reliably and that other people can read if needed

  • Working knowledge of PyTorch and modern ML infrastructure and practices; you are not a pure Python developer, you know what the modern ML code looks like

  • Strong grasp of statistics and its shortcomings in practice, and how to work with those; sample sizes, inter-annotator agreement, confidence levels, etc., and a healthy skepticism about what those numbers say about the world

  • Practical experience with building and operating LLM-as-judge systems, and understanding their limitations

  • Working knowledge of modern benchmarking practices and of standard datasets and benchmarks in the field already; you have an idea of which to trust and which to disregard

  • The inclination to look at the actual outputs your system is judging, and to care about what is there beyond an aggregate score

We'd be especially excited if you:

  • Have practical experience with human evaluation, including study design and execution via panels, and analysis of disagreements and annotator performance

  • Have worked where evaluation meets training (reward models, preference data, RLHF, DPO or similar) and know that whatever you optimize for is what the model learns

  • Have evaluated agentic or multi-step systems and know how hard it is to attribute success or failure to a single step

  • Have built tools that people actually want to use internally

  • Have made public contributions to the field: papers, open source, or otherwise

How We Work Together

We're a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. This role is based in Freiburg, where you'll join us at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week). We'll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we've structured things to make it accessible to all.   • Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

title: Legal AI Engineer (Berlin or Leipzig)
description:
Description

Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.


Your mission

Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.


Your profile

The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
  • No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
  • We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
  • Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
  • Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.
  • Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.


Process

  3. Build session. A live case at the intersection of legal reasoning, prompting, and product work: a real customer scenario, a legal AI workflow, or a playbook that misbehaves.
  4. Meet the team in Leipzig or Berlin.

title: Technical Program Manager
description:
About OLIX

AI is growing faster than any technology in history and the explosion in demand has created a massive infrastructure gap; we can no longer build chips or power stations fast enough to keep up. The industry is still leaning on a ten-year-old hardware blueprint that has reached its limit. A new paradigm that is faster and more efficient will be the biggest economic opportunity of the next century and create the most important company of the next decade. The OLIX Decode Accelerator 1 (DX-1) is the first accelerator architected specifically for decode. Rack-scale co-design of logic, data movement, packaging, optics and interconnect enables a step change in system level performance.

The Role

We are hiring a Technical Program Manager to deliver end-to-end technical program execution across hardware, software, optics and manufacturing - setting the structure, aligning teams, and driving critical programs from R&D through to on-time mass manufactured product delivery.

As Technical Program Manager, you will run a number of programs critical to OLIX’s delivery. You’ll partner closely with engineering to set direction, identify blockers, implement risk mitigations and report on status. You’ll take ownership of cross-functional delivery within your programs, ensuring reliable, high-quality execution in areas critical to OLIX's roadmap.

Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end delivery of complex, cross-functional technical programs from initiation through to completion.

  • Define and maintain program plans, milestones, dependencies, and critical path across multiple workstreams.

  • Drive alignment between engineering, product, and business stakeholders on scope, priorities, and trade-offs.

  • Run structured program cadences: planning sessions, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.

  • Identify, track, and mitigate risks and blockers before they impact delivery.

  • Manage vendor and partner relationships through scope changes, timeline conflicts, and commercial negotiations

  • Maintain clear program documentation: decisions logs, status reports, shared technical information.

  • Hold work stream leads and engineers accountable to commitments without direct line authority.

  • Escalate effectively and concisely when decisions need senior input.

  • Continuously improve delivery processes, tooling, and ways of working across the program.

Skills & Experience

  • Broad engineering background with some technical experience across hardware, software and manufacturing.

  • 3+ years in a TPM, program management, or senior project management role in a technical environment.

  • Proven track record delivering multi-disciplinary programs at scale with multiple interdependent teams.

  • Strong engineering literacy: able to engage credibly on technical trade-offs without being the domain expert.

  • Strong stakeholder management up to VP; comfortable holding people to account

  • Fluent in program management best practices.

  • Structured thinker with high attention to detail and an ability to bring clarity to an otherwise high-ambiguity development environment.

  • Comfortable operating in fast-moving environments.

Compensation & Equity

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience, skills, and location

  • Equity & Ownership: Meaningful stock options. You’re not just joining the mission; you’re owning a piece of it

  • Proximity Bonus: We value your time. To minimise your commute and maximise your life, we offer an annual Living-Local Bonus if your residence is within 20 minutes of the office

  • Retirement Benefits: Employer-contributed retirement plans to help you build long-term financial security

title: Site Reliability Engineer
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We’re hiring Site Reliability Engineers to set the reliability standard across everything we build. You will lead the Infrastructure Solutions team within the wider Technical Operations department. The Operational Reality

It is important to be transparent about the environment you are joining. We operate at high velocity with a broad and complex technology estate. However, we are a lean team, not a giant corporation with endless resources.

  • Context Switching is the Norm
    • You will rarely have the luxury of focusing on a single task for weeks at a time. You will be required to shift focus multiple times a week, and sometimes multiple times a day, as business priorities evolve.
  • Agility over Silos
    • Because we are a lean team, we wear many hats. You must be comfortable pivoting from a strategic discussion to an operational challenge without losing momentum.
  • Focus Management
    • Success in this role requires the ability to maintain high standards while navigating a workload that changes dynamically. This is not a role for those who prefer a slow, singular focus; it is for those who thrive on variety, pace, and solving complex problems in real-time.

 

As the Senior Infrastructure Manager, You Will:

People Leadership & Talent Development

  • Team Management
    • Lead, mentor, and motivate a team of infrastructure engineers. Conduct weekly 1-2-1s, manage performance reviews, and handle all aspects of people management.

    • Foster a "Self-Learner" mindset. Create a transparent environment where failures are treated as learning opportunities and documented as such for future reference.

Strategic & Operational Management

  • Budget & Capacity Planning
    • Ability to own your team's budget and lead capacity planning initiatives. You will forecast future infrastructure needs to ensure we remain scalable while managing spend for subscriptions and hardware.

    • Proactively identify operational risks and form contingency plans immediately to ensure business continuity.
  • Procedure & Frameworks
    • Ability to define, maintain, and cascade operational procedures (SOPs) and ITIL standards.

    • Shield your team from noise by effectively prioritising workloads (Changes, Problems, and Projects) and managing stakeholder expectations.

Technical Support & Oversight

  • Hybrid Estate Management
    • Ability to oversee the management of both On-Premise and Cloud (GCP/AWS), ensuring high availability across all environments.
  • Unblocking Issues
    • Act as the senior escalation point for complex technical issues. Your goal is not to fix the issue yourself, but to coordinate the right resources and provide air cover.

General Duties

On-Call DutiesWillingness to participate in the Management On-Call Rotation to support the department and the business (Current frequency: Once every three weeks). Ad-HocCarry out other strategic or technical duties required to support the Director/VP of Technical Operations.

Essential Knowledge, Skills, and Experience

Leadership & Management Competencies

  • Proven Management Experience
    • Significant experience leading a technical team, with a specific focus on the people management aspect (performance reviews, career growth etc).
  • Project Management
    • Strong project management experience with the ability to delegate effectively to meet tight deadlines. You must be able to multitask and maintain focus in a high-priority environment.
  • Communication
    • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills. You must be able to liaise effectively with management and other business areas. Engagement may also include interactions with senior technical engineers/leaders within other teams and C-Team members. 
  • Goal Oriented
    • You must be highly goal-oriented with strict attention to detail, capable of prioritising workload and demand to ensure targets are met.
  • ITIL Application / Lean Six Sigma
    • Deep knowledge of and experience with ITIL practices, with the ability to apply them to improve team workflows. Demonstrated ability to apply Lean Six Sigma concepts.

 

Technical Environment & Team Capabilities

Focusing on the technical skills that your engineers possess, it would be ideal if you had a decent working knowledge of each of the areas. Hands-on expertise in every area is not required, but the ability to hold and facilitate discussions, know when to push or hold back and when to ask poignant questions will help you effectively mentor the team and guide architectural decisions. 

For reference from above these areas are: on-prem and AWS/GCP solutions; system design from network to application level; resilient database availability strategies; automation and configuration management via Ansible, Docker and CI/CD; programming awareness in Python; Linux administration.

title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Senior Infrastructure Engineer

Remote (UK-based), with occasional on-site work at our data centres | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 50+ of the world’s leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what’s technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer to help run and grow the network and cloud estate behind our trading platform. Networking in our colocation data centres is the core of the role. The estate spans London, New York and Singapore, and from Q1 2027 a new Tokyo data centre.

This is a hands-on role in a small, expert infrastructure team. You’ll work closely with our Head of Infrastructure, following problems from the cross-connect through hosts, containers and AWS. You’ll also help keep infrastructure delivery on track, from timelines and reporting to working closely with our TechOps team.

What You’ll Work On

  • Low-latency networking across our colocation sites: switching and routing, cross-connects, BGP peering with liquidity providers and clients, and the fabric that carries our trading traffic

  • Bringing new sites to application-ready, starting with Tokyo

  • Our hybrid connectivity into multi-region AWS, including Direct Connect, routing and failover

  • Linux hosts and containers on the critical path, with every change made through code (Ansible, Git, Terraform), never by hand

  • Monitoring and alerting that catches problems before clients do, plus runbooks and post-incident reviews that someone else can follow

  • Planning and capacity: forecasting growth, setting timelines and reporting progress to TechOps and engineering

What We Need

  • 4+ years running production infrastructure in a latency-sensitive environment, such as HFT, an exchange, market data or bank trading infrastructure

  • Strong networking: hands-on routing and switching (MLAG, LACP, VLANs), BGP in production, and a solid grasp of low-latency behaviour such as buffers, microbursts and congestion handling

  • Colocation experience: cabinets, cross-connects, remote hands and vendor management

  • Solid Linux (RHEL) and TCP/IP, and the ability to trace a problem from the wire to the application

  • Infrastructure as code and containers as your default way of working

  • Working knowledge of AWS networking, and the confidence to pick up the rest of our stack. Networking depth matters more to us than any particular cloud or platform tooling

  • Methodical, evidence-led troubleshooting and clear documentation

A strong plus:

  • Project management experience: owning timelines, reporting progress, and working with ops teams to hit deadlines

  • Kernel bypass (Onload/ef_vi), PTP and time synchronisation

  • Experience bringing up a new colo site

  • FIX protocol or OTC FX market knowledge

  • Python for tooling

Working pattern: Infrastructure changes are often scheduled outside trading hours, including weekends, and the team shares an on-call rota. We’re a team with flexible hours, so time worked out of hours is taken back during the week. Day-to-day work is remote, with occasional visits to our data centres, most often in London (Slough).

What You Get

  • Real ownership of a live global trading network, hands-on, with few layers of process

  • A build-out year, with a new Tokyo data centre in Q1 and more growth ahead

  • A senior seat in a small, expert team where your changes ship and are measured

  • Competitive package — up to 38 days leave (inc. bank holidays), private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Remote-friendly working with flexibility around out-of-hours work

  • Growth as the estate scales

We believe in transparency, honest feedback and writing things down, and we aim to build systems that don’t depend on the heroics of individuals.

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages:

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition
Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Technical Deep Dive with our Head of Infrastructure
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~90 minutes

Stage 3: Leadership Conversation with our CDO
Format: Video call, ~45 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you’re invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

How to Apply

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you’ll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we’re happy to accommodate.

Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy.

Cyber Security Engineer - Governance Risk & Compliance (GRC) - UK Remote

Immersive is hiring! Could you be our next Cyber Security Engineer?

Due to customer demand and increasing maturity within our platform we have an exciting and challenging opportunity for an experienced cyber professional within the cyber compliance sector - with expertise in conducting governance risk and compliance audits - to join our Product team as Cyber Security Engineer, specialising in Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC).

This isn’t an ordinary GRC role - we know everyone claims this and will tell you their role is super unique…but this one really is.

You are constantly researching, learning, totally geeking out on all things GRC related, from ISO standards, to the latest AI governance, and then taking that knowledge and creating labs and ranges.

You will be a key player in our Cyber team, shaping and influencing the roll out of our offensive security and AI pen test content roadmap, simulating attack paths and helping train our users to counter the latest threats.

You will be educating the world of GRC professionals on how to make sure they are secure in what they do. Now that is a pretty cool legacy to leave behind.

Your mission (if you choose to accept it) is to evolve and disrupt within the governance space by creating emulated environments within our platform that will simulate incidents within highly regulated sectors in an engaging and intuitive way for our community.

You will design, build and deliver practical and theory content to gamify governance, risk and compliance and make it engaging and fun for the end user. You'll shake up traditional training and teach complex concepts in an innovative way.

If you have a passion for cyber security, are experienced in the area of GRC, and want to disrupt how employees build their resilience against the latest threats we will appreciate your input and give you the space to innovate within our market leading platform, Immersive One.

Your main responsibilities (we're scaling fast, so these may change as we grow):

  • Utilising knowledge of Governance, Risk & Compliance to plan, write and improve our security labs, challenges and online learning content on the Immersive One platform.

  • Produce multi-format content utilising various teaching methods; practical exercises, questions & gamification around GRC

  • Peer review cyber labs and ranges to ensure they function as expected

  • Research the latest GRC regulations and standard and compile this research to deliver practical and theory labs to users

  • Compile technical research into understandable concise content for both technical and non-technical audience

  • Act as a GRC subject matter expert for our engineering and product teams, embedding "security and privacy by design" principles into the SDLC

Sounds good? We’d love to hear from you if you have proven experience in the following areas:

  • A number of years of experience working within a heavily regulated industry (e.g., FinTech, Healthcare, or Government), cyber vendor or consultancy. You will have conducted audits and have an understanding of how GRC works in practice and helping companies to comply to these standard

  • In-depth knowledge of the MITRE ATLAS & D3FEND frameworks and how it is used to help enterprises deal with threats to their organisation.

  • Deep understanding of common compliance frameworks and security standards (e.g., NIST SP 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO 27001/27002, SOC 2).

  • Have a strong technical understanding of networking, computing and cyber security concepts

  • Have the ability to use examples and analogies to simplify complex subjects - your content will train real world users to identify and combat the latest threats so you need to be able to inhabit the mindset of your target audience to create realistic simulations

  • Certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CRISC, CISM would be useful to have but not essential

  • Attitude and approach is just as important as technical skills for this role - you will be someone who enjoys tackling complex problems and finding the solution. You'll be a natural problem solver and 'tinkerer' who enjoys prototyping and iteration.

This is a Linux-first, hands-on engineering role. You will not write policies for other people to implement — you will write the Python and Bash that hardens our OS, automates our vulnerability management, and proves to auditors and customers that our supply chain is sound.


About Scality

Scality is the leader in software-defined object storage, trusted by 1,000+ enterprises and 700M+ users worldwide across banking, healthcare, and government sectors — exactly the sectors where security posture is a purchasing criterion, not a checkbox.

Industry recognition:

  • Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for 9 consecutive years — the only 100% software-defined storage company to hold this position since the quadrant’s inception
  • #1 on the GigaOm Radar for Enterprise Object Storage (2024), ahead of 17 competing vendors
  • Gold Stevie Award 2025 — ARTESCA 3.0, Cloud Storage & Backup Solution category
  • Net Promoter Score of 85 across RING and ARTESCA

About the team

You will join a small team of highly skilled Linux engineers responsible for delivering and maintaining ADI (Scality Autonomous Data Infrastructure), our full platform: RING (object storage), S3C (S3-compatible layer), and SCOS (Scality OS — our own Linux distribution).

The team works across the full stack of infrastructure engineering — deep Linux system integration, RPM packaging, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and release automation. The command line is where most of our day happens, and we ship a Linux distribution to customers.


How We Build

We build with AI tools, in earnest rather than as an experiment. Every engineer here has Claude Code, and it is part of how we write, review, and ship code day to day.

We are also designing something larger: an AI code and delivery factory — AI woven into the build and release chain itself, not just into the editor. That work is early and still being thought through rather than already solved. We expect it to become part of how we maintain the platform, and CVE remediation is one of the first places we think it fits: an automated path from advisory to assessment to a patched, tested, delivered build.

If that sounds like a problem you would want to work on, this role sits close to it.

One principle is not negotiable: a human owns the outcome. AI writes code here, and when it does, we own what it produces — the review, the decision to ship, the consequences, and the fix. “The tool did it” is not an explanation we accept from ourselves, and it is not one we would offer a customer. In security work that matters doubly: an answer you cannot defend is worse than no answer at all.


How This Role Works

Scality is building a network of security engineers across the engineering department — a security peer embedded in each development team, rather than a central security function working at arm’s length from the code. You would be that peer for the platform and delivery team.

  • Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering. The agenda is set at that level, with dedicated resources committed across the teams. You will not have to invent it alone — and you will have a voice in it: the engineers closest to the code help decide what goes on the roadmap. We will be straight with you: today security work competes with delivery commitments and too often loses. Naming an owner and funding dedicated people is how we intend to change that. You would help build that capability, not inherit a finished one.
  • The team is accountable for the deliveries. Security items sit on the team’s plate alongside everything else it commits to, rather than in a separate function filing tickets from the outside.
  • You are the dedicated resource that makes them happen. While your teammates carry releases, OS compatibility, and platform features, your time is reserved for the security work. That focus is the whole reason the seat exists.
  • You share the team’s perimeter and its knowledge. Same repositories, same Jira projects, same code reviews, same sprint rituals. The engineers around you have rare, hard-earned Linux depth — OS integration, RPM packaging, boot and GRUB, CI/CD, monitoring — and you will learn the platform from them.
  • You will have peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams work the same problems on different perimeters. That network is where you compare notes, share tooling, and grow into the craft.

    • The point of the model is that security decisions get made inside the team that builds and ships the product, by someone who understands the build system rather than filing tickets against it.


Your First Missions

Two priorities are already on the roadmap, and they will shape your first year.

1. CVE exposure, answered before it is asked

Customers in banking, healthcare, and government ask us, routinely and under their own audit obligations, whether our products are exposed to a given CVE. That will not stop — for them, asking is the compliance requirement. Today each answer is researched from scratch: a customer question becomes a ticket, the ticket becomes a hunt through SBOMs, vendor advisories, and our own configuration, and the round trip can take weeks to produce something the team is not fully confident defending.

Your first mission is to invert that, so the answer already exists when the question arrives.

  • A standing exposure record, per shipped component and per release: what the SBOM says is present, what the upstream vendor has decided (including “will not fix”, which is common on RHEL 8 and often the real answer), and whether the vulnerable code path is actually reachable in our configuration
  • Reachability over presence. A module shipped and loaded by a distribution default is not the same as a module configured on a live URL. That distinction is the difference between “vulnerable” and “no impact”, and it is where the engineering judgement lives
  • Continuous CVE detection across our repositories, vendored third-party modules, container images, and shipped RPMs
  • Wiring detection into our existing SBOM tooling and GitHub Actions pipelines, so exposure is computed when a release is built rather than when a customer asks
  • A defined interface with the security engineers and the customer-facing teams: who produces the technical assessment, who owns the wording that reaches the customer, and how both meet the response commitments in our customer security policy
  • Durable capture. An assessment that lives only in a ticket comment gets re-derived next release. Findings belong somewhere queryable
  • A remediation loop with clear ownership and response targets, integrated with how the team already works in Jira
  • AI-assisted remediation, where it fits: from advisory to proposed patch to a tested build, with a human deciding what ships

    • Done well, a customer’s “are you affected by X?” becomes a lookup and an afternoon, not an escalation and three weeks.

    2. Raising the security baseline of SCOS

    SCOS is our own Linux distribution — we control the kickstarts, the package set, the boot path, and the images. That is unusual leverage, and we intend to use it. You will drive platform-level hardening across the OS we ship:

    • A hardened, defensible default configuration for the distribution
    • Advancing SELinux enforcement across RING and S3C (work already begun on the team, which you will help carry)
    • Supply-chain integrity: artifact provenance, signing, dependency currency, reproducible and verifiable builds
    • Secrets and credential handling across the delivery pipeline
    • Cryptographic posture — including FIPS 140-3 readiness, which matters concretely: FIPS 140-2 certificates move to NIST’s historical list on 22 September 2026, and RHEL 9’s validated OpenSSL, GnuTLS, and kernel crypto modules are the foundation we build on
    • Compliance-driven engineering work, notably the supply-chain security expectations of NIS2 (Article 21(2)(d)) and the EU Cyber Resilience Act — translated into automation and evidence, not spreadsheets

      • You will also contribute to what comes next: threat modelling of the platform, hardening guidance for customers, and security review of significant design changes.


What We Are Looking For

This is a role for someone early in their career who wants to grow into being their team’s security reference. We expect to invest in you, and we expect you to keep growing here for as long as you want to — there is no ceiling built into this seat.

Required

  • Linux is your primary operating system — at work, at home, or both. You are comfortable in the terminal and you reach for a shell before a UI
  • Roughly 2–4 years of relevant experience, or a shorter track record with unusually strong evidence of the skills below
  • Solid working ability in Python and Bash — you will be writing and maintaining real code in a production codebase
  • A genuine, demonstrable interest in security. We care much more about this than about formal credentials. Show it however it is true for you: CTFs, a home lab, reading advisories and CVE writeups for fun, a hardening project, security-adjacent contributions, a blog, anything real
  • Comfortable using Git in a collaborative environment
  • Ability to read and understand existing code before modifying it
  • The judgement to tell a real risk from a scanner’s opinion — and the instinct to check whether vulnerable code is actually reachable before calling it exposed
  • The willingness to say plainly when you are not yet sure, rather than producing an answer you could not defend
  • French — the team works in French day to day
  • Written communication skills in English

    • Nice to Have

    • CVE triage, CVSS scoring, or vulnerability management experience
    • Reading vendor advisories and understanding vendor triage — NVD, RHSA, Red Hat severity and will-not-fix calls
    • Supply-chain security tooling — SBOM formats (SPDX, CycloneDX), scanners (Trivy, Grype, Syft), artifact signing
    • RPM packaging or Linux distribution internals
    • SELinux policy work
    • CI/CD systems, especially GitHub Actions
    • RHEL / Rocky Linux (versions 8 and 9)
    • Containers (Docker, containerd, systemd units)
    • Ansible or Salt
    • Awareness of NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, or FIPS 140-3
    • Familiarity with S3 or object storage concepts
    • Serious use of AI coding tools in a real workflow — Claude Code or equivalent, beyond autocomplete

      • To Be Clear About Scope

      This is a software engineering role with a security mandate. It is not a SOC or incident-response analyst position, not a penetration-testing role, and not a GRC or compliance-documentation role. If what you want is to build the tooling and harden the system yourself, in code, you are in the right place.


What We Offer
  • Dedicated focus. Security is your job here, not the thing you get to after the sprint work is done
  • Clear direction, and a say in it. Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering, and the team is accountable for delivering them. You would not be inventing the agenda on your own, you would help shape what goes on it, and you would be part of making it stick
  • A network of peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams, working the same problems on different perimeters
  • Work that compounds. Customer security questions are a permanent obligation, so every assessment you make reusable and every check you automate keeps paying back, release after release
  • Modern tooling, actually adopted. Claude Code in every engineer’s hands, and a real say in how AI reshapes our build and delivery chain
  • A rare combination: security work with the leverage of owning the whole stack, down to our own Linux distribution
  • Mentorship from senior engineers with deep expertise across Linux, storage, packaging, and distributed systems — you will not be the only person who understands your perimeter
  • A long-term growth path toward becoming your team’s security reference and a senior voice in the network
  • Work that ships to production and runs at exabyte scale, in banking, healthcare, and government
  • Standard French benefits: meal vouchers, Navigo subsidy, mutuelle

title: Account Manager Lille
description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Pourquoi Deliveroo ?

Nous transformons la façon dont le monde mange et fait ses courses en rendant leur accès plus pratique et agréable. Nous connectons les consommateurs, les restaurants, les magasins et les cyclistes. Nous donnons à chaque personne la possibilité d'acheter ce qu'elles veulent, comme elles le veulent, quand elles le veulent et où elles le veulent.

Nous sommes une entreprise axée sur la technologie, à l'avant-garde d'un secteur qui connaît une des expansions les plus rapides au monde. Nous avançons rapidement, valorisons l'autonomie, et sommes toujours en recherche de nouvelles idées et de personnes talentueuses pour nous rejoindre!

Tes principales missions :  

  • Gérer un portefeuille de restaurants clés sur des zones matures, où l'expertise et l'attention au détail font toute la différence.
  • Développer des partenariats privilégiés et durables en devenant le point de contact expert de votre zone et en mettant à profit vos connaissances Food Tech.
  • Optimiser la performance de vos comptes grâce à un accompagnement personnalisé, construit sur le long terme et nourri par la data.
  • Analyser les résultats de vos restaurants, identifier les leviers d'amélioration et recommander des actions concrètes à votre manager tout en restant agile et ouvert à la nouveauté.
  • Proposer et mettre en place des campagnes marketing et promotionnelles ciblées pour booster l'attractivité de vos restaurants partenaires.
  • Suivre de près le déroulé des opérations afin de garantir la meilleure expérience restaurant et client possible.

Ton expérience et tes qualités :

  • Tu as déjà 2 à 3 ans d'expérience sur un rôle similaire où la gestion d'un portefeuille de partenaires était centrale à ta mission.
  • Tu sais négocier et anticiper les discussions commerciales tout en gardant à l'esprit les valeurs de Deliveroo.
  • Tu sais garder le contrôle de ton portefeuille, identifier les nouvelles tendances du marché et partager du feedback utile à tes partenaires ainsi qu'à ton manager.
  • Le terrain est un lieu où tu te sens à ta place : tu sais construire des relations de confiance avec tes partenaires tout en gardant un œil attentif sur la concurrence.
  • Tu sais te montrer proactif, analyser les résultats de tes actions et proposer des recommandations concrètes à ton manager.
  • Tu travailles de manière autonome tout en gardant le cap fixé, sais t'approprier des objectifs précis et mets tout en œuvre pour les atteindre.
  • Tu sais concevoir des actions spécifiques, adaptées à la fois aux besoins de tes partenaires et à la stratégie définie par ton manager.
  • Tu sais identifier, comprendre et analyser les données de performance (commerciales et opérationnelles) pour garantir un niveau de service irréprochable.
  • Tu sais t'exprimer en anglais (à l'oral comme à l'écrit)
  • Tu arrives à convaincre tout en construisant des relations commerciales solides, durables, où Deliveroo devient le partenaire de choix
  • Et si tu cherches un poste où tu travailles en full remote depuis Lille, tout en gardant un lien fort avec le terrain et les équipes, alors c'est peut‑être le rôle qu'il te faut !

La vie chez Deliveroo

Notre équipe est en forte croissance, notre impact très important, et nous cherchons à répondre aux questions les plus stimulantes du moment. Nous progressons rapidement, nous explorons toujours de nouvelles idées et nous sommes très transparents quant aux décisions que nous prenons et à ce qui motive nos choix.

Il y a tellement de questions que nous souhaitons résoudre, et encore plus que nous n'avons pas encore rencontrées. Comment les données et la technologie peuvent-elles aider les restaurants à développer leur activité à mesure que les habitudes des consommateurs évoluent ? Comment pouvons-nous prédire ce qu'une personne souhaitera pour dîner avant même que l'idée ne lui vienne à l'esprit ? Chez Deliveroo, ces questions ne sont que quelques-uns des défis ambitieux auxquels nous nous efforçons de répondre – et il n'y a aucun projet qui ne peut pas devenir le vôtre. Aucune solution n'appartient à une équipe en particulier, ce qui vous ouvre d'extraordinaires possibilités en termes de développement et d'impact personnel.

Avantages et diversité

À compétences égales, ce poste est ouvert aux travailleurs et travailleuses en situation de handicap ou assimilés au sens de l'article L5212-13 du Code du travail. Deliveroo s'engage en faveur de la diversité, l'égalité professionnelle, l'emploi des personnes en situation de handicap.

Deliveroo France valorise la diversité sans discrimination de genre, race, sexualité, religion ou préférences personnelles. Avec un score de 99/100 à l'Indice de l'Égalité Hommes-Femmes 2023, nous sommes engagés envers l'égalité des chances. Rejoignez-nous avec votre passion pour la nourriture dans une entreprise en pleine croissance.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!


Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness.

On our most strategic accounts, Deployment Strategists in our Forward Deployed Engineering team already build account-specific business cases and ROI narratives as part of delivery. You will partner with them rather than duplicate that work. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.

This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. Au sein du Département Automatique, Productique et Informatique, le poste sera associé à l’équipe TASC (Théorie, Algorithmes et Systèmes en Contraintes ) dont les thématiques de recherche s’articulent autour de la programmation par contraintes, de la théorie aux applications en passant par l’hybridation. Dans ce cadre, le poste a pour objectif de venir en soutien au développement du solveur de contraintes choco-solver (http://choco-solver.org) maintenu par l’équipe TASC.

 

MISSIONS

Sous la responsabilité fonctionnelle du responsable du projet et développeur principal de la plateforme Choco-solver et en collaboration avec les membres de l’équipe TASC, les missions principales du poste sont :

  1.   Adapter l’algorithme bimodal aux contraintes reposant sur des parcours en profondeur, telles que GlobalCardinality, StableKeysort ou Circuit ;

  2.   Étudier la transposition des bénéfices de l’approche bimodale au cœur d’un solveur de contraintes (p. ex. le moteur de propagation) ;

  3.   Évaluer l’impact des explications paresseuses (lazy) dans les contraintes Sum et AllDifferent, entre autres ;

  4.   Participer à la rédaction d’articles scientifiques liés à ces sujets.

 

 ACTIVITÉS : Activité par mission

2.      Étudier la transposition des bénéfices de l’approche bimodale au cœur d’un solveur de contraintes

·       Étudie le fonctionnement interne de choco-solver (moteur de propagation, ordonnancement des propagateurs, gestion des événements) afin d’identifier les mécanismes pouvant tirer parti d’une stratégie bimodale

·       Propose et prototype une ou plusieurs adaptations, par exemple un basculement dynamique entre modes de propagation

·       Évalue expérimentalement ces prototypes et analyse les compromis entre coût et bénéfice

 

3.      Évaluer l’impact des explications paresseuses (

·       Implémente ou étend la génération paresseuse d’explications pour les contraintes Sum, AllDifferent et d’autres contraintes globales

title: Alternant·e Growth Marketing Manager | Thiga Academy
description:
Alternance · Paris 9e · Télétravail · rythme d’alternance souhaité 3 semaines entreprise / 1 semaine école 
 
Thiga en 30 secondes : 

Thiga est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en IA et en digital. Nous accompagnons les plus grands groupes et scale-ups françaises : Decathlon, Doctolib, AXA, ManoMano, Mirakl, Disney, Leboncoin et une centaine d'autres. Nous sommes 200, majoritairement à Paris.
Thiga Academy, c'est notre organisme de formation. On y forme les équipes produit (Product Managers, Product Owners, Designers, Product Leaders) et celles qui veulent le devenir : product management, product discovery, leadership produit, et IA appliquée au produit. En inter-entreprise comme en intra, on transmet ce que nos consultants pratiquent chez nos clients tous les jours
 
Pourquoi ce poste : 

L'Academy forme chaque année 2000 professionnels et son offre est solide. Le problème : aujourd'hui, elle ne communique presque pas. Peu de contenu, peu de présence, une notoriété très en dessous de ce que le catalogue mérite.

C'est une page blanche côté growth, et c'est exactement ce qui rend le poste intéressant. On cherche quelqu'un pour construire, mesurer et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition de l'Academy à partir de zéro : quels canaux, quels messages, quel funnel, avec quels résultats. Pas pour décorer le catalogue, pour le remplir.


Ce que tu vas faire 🖇

1. Construire et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition, avec le Head of Marketing & Events

  • Structurer le tunnel d'acquisition de bout en bout : quels canaux amènent du trafic, ce qui convertit en lead, ce qui déclenche l'inscription

  • Tester des canaux et des formats en continu (LinkedIn organique et payant, email, SEO, partenariats, salons) et couper vite ce qui ne marche pas

  • Créer et itérer les landing pages du catalogue et des sessions, pensées pour convertir dès le premier jet et retravaillées à partir de la donnée

  • Mettre en place les séquences email dans HubSpot : nurturing, relances, réactivation des contacts dormants, avec un test A/B sur les objets et les CTA

  • Accompagner le lancement des nouvelles formations avec un plan d'acquisition dédié, pas seulement un plan de com

  • Créer les supports nécessaires au tunnel avec Figma (catalogue, plaquettes, brochures) en gardant en tête qu'un support existe pour convertir, pas pour exister

  • Représenter l'Academy sur des salons et événements, avec un objectif de leads qualifiés en sortie, pas juste de présence

    • 2. Mesurer, analyser, arbitrer

    Le nerf du poste. Sans mesure, pas de growth, juste du marketing qui se raconte des histoires.

  • Suivre les KPIs qui comptent à chaque étape du tunnel : trafic, taux de clic, taux de conversion en lead, taux de conversion en inscrit, coût d'acquisition par inscrit, taux de remplissage des sessions

  • Construire les dashboards HubSpot qui donnent une vision claire de ce qui marche, canal par canal, campagne par campagne

  • Identifier où le tunnel fuit et proposer les hypothèses à tester pour colmater

  • Faire remonter les résultats au Head of Marketing & Events pour arbitrer les prochains messages, offres et canaux, avec des chiffres, pas des impressions

    • 3. Faire vivre la marque et la communauté qui nourrissent le funnel

    L'acquisition ne marche pas sans contenu ni preuve sociale. C'est le carburant du tunnel.

  • Poser la ligne éditoriale et la faire vivre : posts LinkedIn, articles, newsletters, formats courts autour du product et de l'IA

  • Animer la relation avec les alumni et la communauté d'apprenants : témoignages, cas concrets, un bouche-à-oreille qu'on peut transformer en canal d'acquisition mesurable

    • L'IA n'est pas une option chez nous, c'est la pierre angulaire de notre façon de travailler, et on attend de toi que tu aies cette fibre. Concrètement, tu t'appuieras sur l'IA à chaque étape : générer et itérer des variantes de copies avec Claude, produire des visuels avec Nano Banana et Figma, des teasers avec HeyGen, ou transformer une transcription Granola en article et en carrousel LinkedIn. C'est ce qui te permet d'avancer vite et de tester dix fois plus d'hypothèses qu'une équipe classique.


    La stack que tu vas pratiquer 🧰

    Le growth marketing moderne, c'est une combinaison d'intuition testée par la donnée, de vitesse d'exécution et de bons outils au bon moment.

  • LLM et agents : Claude (Pro et Code), Gemini

  • Génération visuelle et audio : Nano Banana, Adobe Firefly, ElevenLabs, HeyGen

  • Marketing ops : HubSpot (CRM, marketing hub, workflows), Luma, Phantom Buster

  • Prise de notes et capitalisation : Granola, Notion AI

  • Vibe coding (en bonus, pour les profils qui veulent aller plus loin) : Lovable, Cursor pour bricoler des micro-outils internes

    • Tu n'as pas besoin de tout maîtriser à l'arrivée. On attend une vraie curiosité et l'envie de pratiquer, pas un CV exhaustif.


    Le profil que nous recherchons 🌟

  • Formation : école de commerce ou de communication, en M1 ou M2, idéalement avec une spécialisation marketing, growth ou entrepreneuriat

  • Pratique IA personnelle prouvée : tu as un side project, un compte ChatGPT ou Claude que tu utilises tous les jours, un workflow Make ou n8n que tu as construit, un agent custom, un blog assisté par LLM, un repo GitHub, ou n'importe quoi qui démontre que l'IA est dans ta vie.

  • Réflexe growth : tu penses en funnel avant de penser en campagne, tu formules des hypothèses avant de produire, et tester puis mesurer te vient plus naturellement que produire pour produire

  • Appétence data : Excel ou Google Sheets n'ont pas de secret pour toi, et l'idée de creuser un dashboard pour comprendre pourquoi un taux de conversion a bougé t'intéresse plus qu'elle ne t'ennuie

  • Fibre communication : tu sais écrire pour être lu, tu as déjà animé une page, un compte ou une communauté

  • Rigueur opérationnelle et sens du détail : tu sais qu'une séquence email qui commence par « Bonjour {prénom} », ça fait tâche, et qu'un A/B test mal cadré ne prouve rien

  • Sensibilité business : tu comprends les concepts MQL, CAC, NPS, et tu sais qu'une belle campagne ne vaut rien si elle ne remplit pas les sessions

    • Au-delà des hard skills, on recherche surtout quelqu’un de curieux, volontaire, débrouillard et qui n’a pas peur de proposer des nouvelles idées !


    Ce qu'on offre 🎊

  • Stack IA premium : Claude, Gemini, et accès facilité à tous les outils IA quand ils sont pertinents pour ton travail

  • Encadrement et présence au quotidien de membres de l'équipe marketing pointus sur les sujets growth, événementiel et IA

  • Cadence de suivi : 1-to-1 hebdomadaire avec le Head of Marketing & Events. Fonctionnement quotidien en équipe avec les autres Head of (Content, Design) et le CMO

  • Cadre de travail : bureaux 23 rue Taitbout (Paris 9), équipe marketing de 8 personnes

  • Rémunération : grille légale alternance, transparente dès l'entretien

    Envoie ton CV, un lien vers un side project ou portfolio (même bricolé). Pas de lettre de motivation.

  • Un premier call avec notre Talent Acquisition Manager

description:

moka.care is a mental health solution for companies, with one mission in mind: nurturing healthy minds to foster healthy organizations.

We guide employees through individual and group therapy or coaching sessions.

Alongside we help HR teams to take care of their employees’ mental health on a daily basis.

Where we are currently: Since our creation in December 2019, more than 400 companies (L'Oreal, Spendesk, Qonto, Engie, Castalie, etc.) have joined moka.care, and we now have over 300,000 employees covered in France but also throughout the world!

We have raised 17,5 million euros and are 70 to help companies improve their mental well-being.

What we believe in? Excellence in care is our obsession.

Culture is not nice words we put on the walls, we have defined 4 tangible values to make this culture live: Team Play, Optimism, Ownership & Agility.

Moka.Care has built strong foundations in a rapidly evolving market. We are now looking for a marketing leader who can scale our growth and pipeline generation efforts, strengthen our commercial execution, improve go-to-market effectiveness and continue building a leading brand for HR and People teams.

  • Brand, Awareness & Customer Enablement, led by a Brand & Product Marketing Lead
  • Lead Generation, Content & Sales Enablement
  • BDR Team, led by a BDR Team Lead

  • You combine strategic thinking with a strong operational mindset

  • You know how to build strong alignment between Marketing, BDR, Sales and Revenue Operations teams

title: AI Harness Engineer - Agentic & Autonomous Operations (m/f/x)
description:
xHeron is building the Service-as-Software company for short-term rental operators. We take responsibility for guest communication, team coordination and issue resolution, so customers can hand over the work without handing over their business.

Today, we deliver that service through people, software and AI. We’re turning the expertise behind it into autonomous systems that understand situations, take action and follow through. Not another tool to supervise. A service that gets the job done.

We’re looking for an AI Engineer to build the agentic capabilities at the heart of xHeron. You’ll help shape how our agents reason, act and learn, and build a company where AI doesn’t just support the work, but increasingly delivers it.

Tasks

We are looking for an AI Harness Engineer to build the software layer that turns language models into dependable operational systems.

You will work on orchestration, context assembly, tool execution, state, permissions, evaluations, observability, failure recovery, and human handoffs. The goal is not merely to generate a good response.

What You’ll Own

  • Agent harness architecture: Build the control layer around models: task decomposition, state management, model and tool selection, execution loops, checkpoints, retries, stopping conditions, and human handoffs.
  • Decision and execution behavior: Design how agents interpret situations, choose actions, manage uncertainty, and complete bounded operational tasks—not only how they generate text.
  • Context and memory: Determine what an agent needs to know at each step. Build context assembly, retrieval, memory, evidence selection, and knowledge-maintenance strategies while managing relevance, latency, and cost.
  • Tools and real-world effects: Connect agents to APIs and operational systems through explicit tool contracts, permissions, validation, idempotency, and confirmation that the intended effect actually occurred.
  • Evaluation and regression testing: Build representative evaluation suites and automated tests for decision quality, tool use, task completion, safety, escalation behavior, and recurring failure patterns.
  • Observability and failure analysis: Make agent behavior inspectable through structured traces, state, outcomes, and error classification. Diagnose failures across models, prompts, context, tools, and surrounding software.
  • Continuous improvement: Use evaluations, production traces, operator feedback, and controlled experiments to improve prompts, context, tools, model choices, and agent architecture.
  • Production ownership: Ship and operate production Python software alongside our CTO and engineering team. Work closely with systems engineering on integrations, authorization, durable state, recovery, and safe execution.

Requirements

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You are a strong software engineer who can design, build, test, and operate reliable production systems in Python.
  • You have built a substantial LLM-powered, automation, workflow, or decision system: not only notebooks, chat interfaces, prompt experiments, or a basic retrieval pipeline.
  • You understand the engineering layer around a model: orchestration, state, context, tools, structured outputs, permissions, retries, fallbacks, observability, and evaluations.
  • You can connect intelligence to real work: selecting relevant evidence, making a bounded decision, invoking tools or APIs, and verifying that the intended result occurred.
  • You design for partial failure and uncertainty. You think deliberately about when an agent should act, retry, wait, stop, ask for help, or escalate.
  • You evaluate behavior systematically. You use representative cases, traces, outcome checks, comparisons, and regression tests rather than treating a plausible response as proof of success.
  • You have shipped software that people or operational processes depend on and have worked through debugging, timeouts, inconsistent data, changing APIs, and production incidents.
  • You can investigate ambiguous problems independently, define a useful system boundary, explain trade-offs clearly, and turn decisions into working software.
  • You care about simplicity and control. You know when a deterministic workflow is better than an agent and when additional autonomy is justified by evidence.
  • You bring useful expertise and an independent perspective. Strong adjacent experience in workflow engines, developer tooling, distributed systems, automation platforms, or integration-heavy backend software can be highly relevant when paired with credible LLM-system understanding.

Around 2+ years of professional software-engineering experience is a useful guide, not a hard requirement. What matters is the technical depth of what you built, the decisions and production outcomes you owned, and your ability to learn unfamiliar systems.

You May Not Be a Great Fit If

  • Your LLM experience is mainly prompt engineering, chatbots, basic RAG, or connecting a model API to a user interface.
  • Your background is primarily offline data analysis, model training, or experimentation, and you do not want to own production software and operational behavior.
  • You treat retrieval as the complete agent architecture rather than one possible source of context within a larger execution system.
  • You consider a coherent model response successful without verifying the decision, tool call, state change, or real-world outcome.
  • You rely on an agent framework to provide the system design and are not comfortable reasoning about the control flow, state, permissions, and failure behavior underneath it.
  • You are not interested in owning evaluations, trace analysis, regression testing, and production learning alongside feature development.
  • You prefer fully scoped implementation tasks with stable requirements and limited responsibility for product or operational outcomes.

Benefits

Real ownership: you're not maintaining someone else's codebase, you're building a core, novel part of the product from the ground up.

  • Build at the core. Own a defining part of xHeron’s technology, from the first architectural decisions to production.
  • Shape the direction. Work directly with our CTO, challenge assumptions and help decide what we build, not just how.
  • Grow beyond the job description. We invest in your development, with room to expand your ownership and take on technical leadership as xHeron grows.
  • Share in the upside. Salary plus VSOP participation, so you can benefit from the value you help create.

Our Process

  • Intro call (15-30 min): a conversation with Friedrich (CTO) about your background, what you've built, and why this role.
  • Technical take-home case study: a short, real engineering problem, close to what you'd actually be building.
  • Case study interview (1 hour): you walk us through your thinking, not just the final code.
  • Culture fit (30 min): meet both Founders and make sure it's a fit both ways.

Our platform sits between our customers and dozens of third-party accounting and ERP systems. That makes reliability part of our product. Metrics, logs, traces and alerts, across our services and the third-party APIs we call. You’ll define what “healthy” means, build the dashboards, and set up alerting and on-call so we catch problems before our clients do. description:

At Apex.AI, we develop safety-certified software for mobility systems and intelligent machines. Our products power applications in automotive, trucking, robotics, aerospace, agriculture, industrial automation, and defense systems.

We are hiring a Senior DevOps Engineer to design and scale Apex.AI's build and release systems. You will architect and implement our build and release system solutions, which impact developer productivity company-wide and ensure that customers receive high-quality products in a timely manner.

    • Apex.AI is an international software company specializing in the development of safety-certified, developer-friendly, and scalable software for mobility systems, aiming to accelerate the transition to software-defined vehicles and mobility. Founded in 2017 by Jan Becker and Dejan Pangercic, the company is headquartered in Palo Alto, California, with additional offices in Munich, Stuttgart, Gothenburg, Tokyo, and Pangyo. To date, Apex.AI has raised over $75 million USD from world-class venture, financial and strategic investors including AGCO, Airbus Ventures, Canaan, Continental AG, Daimler Truck, HELLA Ventures, Jaguar Land Rover’s InMotion Ventures, LG Electronics, Lightspeed, Orillion, Toyota Ventures, Volvo Group Venture Capital and ZF.

title: Data Scientist - Broker Flow
description:
Data Scientist - Broker Flow Team

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom

We're looking for a Data Scientist to join the Broker Flow team.

You'll own the experiments that shape the journey brokers use to apply on their clients' behalf. Brokers are one of iwoca's main routes to new customers.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

Broker Flow, a new team in iwoca's third-party acquisition department, owns the journey for businesses that come to iwoca through a broker – from before they apply to a completed credit assessment. Its aim is to get more of those businesses to an offer. Broker Terms, a separate team, then sets the price, amount, and duration of each offer.

The team works on three parts of that journey:

  • Broker engagement. Working with brokers and their clients before an application starts.

  • The application. Making it smooth to complete, and collecting the data a credit decision needs.

  • Operations. Running the CRM tools iwoca's teams work in, and automating operational processes.

The team is small and cross-functional – commercial strategy, engineering, design, and data science – and works across the full application stack, from the Broker API to the Introducer Portal brokers use.

The role

As the Data Scientist in Broker Flow, you'll give the team the evidence behind its product decisions. The core of the work is experiment design and causal inference, with modelling and analysis alongside it.

You'll own each project end to end. You'll frame the problem, choose the method, build the model or run the test, and take the answer to the commercial and strategy colleagues who act on it. You'll also meet brokers in person, which gives you the context to ask the right questions. The team is new, so its methods are yours to shape. You'll see the effect of your work in how many businesses reach an offer, and in their lifetime value.

You'll work with data scientists in iwoca's other broker and partner teams, and join the analytics guild – iwoca's data science community – to compare methods and build your expertise. Your results reach the wider business through Learnings, short write-ups that iwoca shares at weekly and fortnightly sessions.

Live project examples:

  • Refinancing. Modelling which businesses would benefit from refinancing their existing borrowing, and testing a product for them.

  • Stalled applications. Finding where broker applications stall, and testing fixes – from clearer emails and portal updates to an early offer that encourages document upload.

  • Reintroductions. Testing the best moment for brokers to bring existing iwoca customers back to borrow.

  • Approval probability. Measuring how well the estimate brokers see in the Introducer Portal predicts actual credit decisions, and making it more accurate.

  • Measuring impact. Designing early signals – at sign-up and once documents are in – that predict a business's lifetime value, so the team can judge its changes quickly.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field such as mathematics, physics, or statistics. You're comfortable with Bayesian reasoning, and have applied hierarchical models or formal decision-making under uncertainty in real work.

  • Causal inference and experimentation. You've separated signal from noise in observational and experimental data. You know where A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead.

  • Analytical ownership. You take loosely defined problems from start to finish – framing the question, choosing the method, and landing the answer with the people who act on it.

  • Data tooling. You're proficient with data manipulation and modelling tools, and with scientific computing libraries.

  • AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – an analysis pipeline, a prototype, or a tool others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't, and you check its output before anyone acts on it.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail for non-technical colleagues in commercial and strategy roles.

Bonus:

  • Modelling depth. You've built or adapted statistical or ML models and can explain the maths behind them.

  • Stochastic methods. You've used stochastic processes for inference or time-series modelling.

  • Broker market insight. You've worked with brokers or other intermediaries in lending or financial services.

  • Coding. You can write code for analysis. The team works in Python.

The salary

We expect to pay from £70,000 to £100,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits
