title: Product Designer (m/f/d) — Energy Insights
description:
What we are building

ecoplanet gives industrial companies the kind of energy management a corporate energy department would provide, without needing one of their own. We work with German Mittelstand manufacturers in plastics, metals, and food production, helping them see where their energy goes, catch problems when they happen, and act on what they find. Our platform covers meter data, consumption monitoring, efficiency analysis, compliance, and energy procurement. We're a Series A company backed by EQT Ventures and HV Capital.


Why This Role Matters

You'll be the designer on our Energy Insights team. The team owns our core entry product: 24/7 consumption monitoring, alerting, and the insights that turn load profiles into decisions a customer can act on. Your work covers the whole customer journey, from onboarding and labelling a customer's meters, to surfacing findings they can trust, to making sure they come back regularly.

You'll be the only designer on this team, working directly with a PM, engineers, and our customer success team. Much of the work is improving and reshaping features we already have, so you'll be making existing things clearer and more useful as well as designing new ones.


What You’ll Achieve

  • Own design for the Energy Insights product end to end: research, flows, interaction design, and polished UI
  • Redesign existing features, such as the customer cockpit, monitoring views, alerts, and findings, so energy managers can go from "something's off" to "here's what to do" quickly
  • Design data-dense interfaces (load profiles, consumption breakdowns, anomalies) that stay readable for people who aren't data analysts
  • Shape onboarding and labelling flows that help customers describe their meters and production so our insights improve over time
  • Design internal tools for our customer success and onboarding teams. They're users too.
  • Talk to customers regularly and turn what you learn into design decisions
  • Help build and maintain a pragmatic design system that fits how we ship


What Sets You Up for Success

Must have:

  • B2B product design experience — you've designed complex software for professional users, not only consumer apps
  • A portfolio showing data-heavy, workflow-driven product work, and the reasoning behind it
  • Comfort working as a solo designer: you set your own process, make calls without waiting for sign-off, and know when "good enough to learn from" beats "perfect"
  • An early-stage mindset — priorities shift as we learn, and you treat ambiguity as something to work through, not around
  • Strong interaction and visual design skills; fluent in Figma
  • Willingness to talk to users directly and bring evidence into design discussions
  • Clear communication in English; German at a professional working level, since most of our customers operate in German and you'll need to understand their feedback directly
Nice to have:
  • Experience with industrial, manufacturing, energy, IoT, or other operational software
  • Familiarity with time-series data, dashboards, or monitoring and alerting products
  • Some front-end understanding — enough to work closely with engineers on feasibility and detail


How You’ll Grow

As the sole designer on a core product team, you'll set the design practice for Energy Insights largely on your own terms — there's no senior designer above you dictating process. You'll work closely enough with customers and engineers to see the direct consequences of your decisions, and as the product and team grow, you'll have the option to shape whether and how a design function scales beyond you.


What You Get

  • Real ownership: your designs define how industrial customers experience the product
  • Direct impact on a product that helps companies cut energy waste and costs
  • A small, senior-leaning team with short decision paths and close access to customers
  • Top-of-market team, flat hierarchy — work alongside people who push you to get better
  • Central office, easy commute — free lunch every Tuesday and Thursday
  • Wellpass membership
  • Regular 1:1s and retros focused on your growth
  • Hybrid setup based in our Munich office, with regular in-person days alongside the team


The Application

Send us your CV and portfolio — we don't do long forms or generic cover letters. Surprise us.

About Doctorflix

Doctorflix ist die digitale Plattform, auf der Ärzte im deutschsprachigen Raum lernen: kostenlos, zertifiziert und mit dem größten Angebot im Markt. Weil wir dort sind, wo Ärzte ihr Wissen auf den neuesten Stand bringen, sind wir auch der Kanal, über den Pharma- und MedTech-Unternehmen sie relevant erreichen. Unsere Vision: die führende Plattform für medizinisches Wissen zu werden, zuerst in DACH, dann international. Ein Ort, an dem Ärzte lernen, sich austauschen und bessere Entscheidungen für ihre Patienten treffen. Wir sind ein VC-finanziertes Startup aus Berlin und wachsen organisch wie anorganisch.


Role

Wir sind aus der frühen Startup-Phase herausgewachsen: ein neues Sales-Team, neue Produkte, anorganisches Wachstum in Vorbereitung, der Schritt ins Ausland in Sicht. Was uns jetzt bremst, sind nicht fehlende Ideen, sondern Prozesse, die nicht mitwachsen.

Als Chief of Staff arbeitest du direkt mit unseren Gründern Hans und Leo und machst aus Strategie ein laufendes System. Du baust unsere Operations so um, dass sie bei doppelter Größe noch funktionieren, automatisierst, was kein Mensch mehr tun sollte, und übernimmst die Projekte, die über unser nächstes Jahr entscheiden.

Das ist weder eine Assistenzrolle noch ein reiner Strategie-Job. Du schreibst nicht die Folie über den Prozess. Du baust den Prozess und, wo es Sinn ergibt, den Agenten, der ihn ausführt.


Your tasks

Operations & Organisation für Scale

  • Du nimmst unsere Kernprozesse auseinander (Angebot bis Rechnung, Kampagnen-Go-live, Content-Produktion, Reporting) und baust sie neu: klare Ownership, saubere Übergaben, messbare Durchlaufzeiten.
  • Du etablierst unseren Operating Rhythm: OKR-Prozess mit Owner pro Key Result, Leadership-Meetings, KPI-Reviews, nachvollziehbare Entscheidungen.
  • Du professionalisierst die Organisation: Rollen und Verantwortlichkeiten, ein Tool-Stack, der zusammenspielt (ClickUp, Notion, Metabase, CRM), und genau die Regeln, die wir brauchen. Nicht mehr.
  • Gemeinsam mit Finance und externen Partnern machst du Backoffice-Prozesse wie Rechnungsstellung, Forderungsmanagement und Abschluss-Zulieferung robust.

Automatisierung & AI-Workflows

  • Du verantwortest unsere AI-native-Agenda: In jedem Team identifizierst du die Workflows mit dem größten Hebel, automatisierst sie und misst die Wirkung (Zeit, Fehlerquote, Durchlaufzeit).
  • Du baust selbst: Agenten und Automationen mit LLM-APIs (z. B. Claude), n8n, Make oder Zapier, Skripten und Schnittstellen zwischen unseren Systemen. Bei größeren Vorhaben steuerst du Product und Engineering.
  • Du sorgst dafür, dass jede Automation dokumentiert ist, überwacht wird und einen Owner hat, statt nach drei Monaten still kaputtzugehen.

Strategische Sonderprojekte

  • M&A & Post-Merger-Integration: Du begleitest Zukäufe von der Due Diligence bis zur Integration. Teams, Kunden, Plattformen, Inhalte und Prozesse führst du mit einem 100-Tage-Plan und klaren Synergiezielen zusammen.
  • Internationalisierung: Du bereitest den Markteintritt außerhalb von DACH vor: Business Case, Markt- und Partneranalyse, operatives Playbook.
  • Themen, die heute niemand im Team ownt, die aber jemand ownen muss.

Führung

  • Du führst Teams und Projektgruppen bereichsübergreifend, je nach Phase auch interimistisch, etwa ein integriertes Team nach einem Zukauf.
  • Du forderst Teamleads heraus, ambitionierte Ziele zu setzen, und hältst nach, dass sie erreicht werden.

Fundraising & Investor Relations

  • Du unterstützt die Gründer bei Finanzierungsrunden: Equity Story, Finanzmodell, Datenraum, Due-Diligence-Fragen.
  • Du verantwortest Board-Unterlagen und das monatliche Investoren-Reporting inhaltlich mit.


Your profile

  • Operator: Mindestens 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung, davon mehrere Jahre in operativer Verantwortung, z. B. in Operations, BizOps oder Founder's Office eines Scale-ups, als Gründer oder nach einem Start in Beratung, PE oder VC mit Wechsel ins Operative. title: Junior Talent Acquisition Partner (m/w/d)
description:
Davon träumen wir:

Mehr als Recruiting. Die richtigen Menschen für die richtigen Aufgaben.
 
VielfaltMenü befindet sich in einer Phase der Weiterentwicklung. Wir schärfen unsere Organisation, professionalisieren unsere Prozesse und richten uns noch konsequenter auf unsere Kund:innen, unsere Mitarbeiter:innen und nachhaltiges Wachstum aus.
Dazu gehört auch ein neues Verständnis von Recruiting.
Wir wollen Stellen nicht einfach besetzen. Wir wollen verstehen, welche Kompetenzen wir wirklich benötigen, wie wir sie erkennen und welche Menschen zu unserer Organisation und unseren Zielen passen.

Dafür suchen wir dich als Junior Talent Acquisition Partner:in

Du musst nicht bereits zehn Jahre Recruiting-Erfahrung mitbringen. 
Entscheidend sind für uns analytisches Denken, Neugier, ein ausgeprägter Qualitätsanspruch und die Fähigkeit, Menschen und Kompetenzen gut einzuschätzen.
  
Deine Aufgaben
Du begleitest Recruitingprozesse von der ersten Anforderungsanalyse bis zum unterschriebenen Arbeitsvertrag und entwickelst gemeinsam mit People & Culture unsere Recruitingstandards weiter.
Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unseren Führungskräften und der Geschäftsführung zusammen.
Talent Acquisition & Beratung
Du führst strukturierte Briefings mit Führungskräften und übersetzt Anforderungen in klare Kompetenz- und Kandidatenprofile.
Du berätst Führungskräfte bei der Auswahl geeigneter Kandidat:innen und sprichst auch dann eine klare Empfehlung aus, wenn die einfachste Lösung nicht die beste ist.
Interviews führst du eigenständig – vom operativen Recruiting bis hin zu Gesprächen auf Managementebene.
Kompetenzorientierte Auswahl
Wir wollen Auswahlentscheidungen stärker auf Kompetenzen und nachvollziehbare Kriterien stützen.
Du entwickelst strukturierte Interviewleitfäden, Bewertungsmatrizen und Auswahlstandards und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Entscheidungen vergleichbarer und belastbarer werden.
Bei diagnostischen Auswahlverfahren und Assessments begleitest du Konzeption, Durchführung und Auswertung.
Dein Anspruch dabei: weniger Bauchgefühl, mehr Qualität in der Entscheidung.
Candidate Experience & Kreativität
Professionelle Prozesse dürfen trotzdem persönlich sein.
Du entwickelst Ideen, wie wir Kandidat:innen besser erreichen und ihnen vom ersten Kontakt bis zur Einstellung eine überzeugende Candidate Experience bieten.
Dabei probierst du neue Recruitingwege aus, hinterfragst bestehende Prozesse und entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns moderne Recruitingformate.
Vertragsmanagement & Prozesse
Du steuerst den Recruitingprozess zuverlässig bis zum Vertragsabschluss.
Du bereitest Vertragsangebote vor, koordinierst Abstimmungen und sorgst dafür, dass Vereinbarungen vollständig, korrekt und termingerecht umgesetzt werden.
Arbeitsrechtliche und datenschutzrechtliche Fragestellungen erkennst du und kannst sie gemeinsam mit People & Culture bzw. unserer juristischen Expertise einordnen.
Du arbeitest strukturiert, standardisiert und detailgenau – ohne dabei unnötige Bürokratie aufzubauen.
 
Was du mitbringst
Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium, beispielsweise in Wirtschaftspsychologie, Psychologie, Personalmanagement, Wirtschafts- oder Rechtswissenschaften, oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.
Erste praktische Erfahrung im Recruiting, Talent Acquisition, HR oder in der Personalauswahl ist hilfreich – beispielsweise durch Werkstudententätigkeiten, Praktika oder deine erste berufliche Station.
Auch wenn du am Anfang deiner Karriere stehst, freuen wir uns ausdrücklich auf deine Bewerbung.
Wichtiger als die Anzahl deiner Berufsjahre ist für uns, wie du denkst und arbeitest.
Du hast Interesse an eignungsdiagnostischen und kompetenzorientierten Auswahlverfahren.
Du kannst Gespräche strukturieren, genau zuhören, kritisch nachfragen und deine Einschätzung anschließend nachvollziehbar begründen.
Du hast ein gutes Verständnis für wirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge und keine Scheu davor, mit Führungskräften und Geschäftsführung auf Augenhöhe zu diskutieren.
Juristische Fragestellungen – insbesondere rund um Arbeitsverträge und Arbeitsrecht – schrecken dich nicht ab. Idealerweise bringst du bereits entsprechende Grundkenntnisse mit.
Du arbeitest sehr sorgfältig und hast gleichzeitig Freude daran, Dinge neu zu denken.
 

Was uns bei dir besonders wichtig ist
Kreativität. 
Du akzeptierst nicht automatisch, dass Recruiting so funktionieren muss, wie es schon immer funktioniert hat.
Struktur. 
Du glaubst an Standards, klare Prozesse und nachvollziehbare Entscheidungen.
Detailorientierung.  
Ein falsches Datum im Arbeitsvertrag ist für dich keine Kleinigkeit.
Urteilsvermögen.
Du möchtest verstehen, welche Kompetenzen jemand wirklich mitbringt – und nicht nur, wie gut sich jemand präsentieren kann.
Mut zur Empfehlung.
Von dir erwarten wir nicht nur Organisation. Wir wollen deine Einschätzung hören.
Neugier.
Du möchtest verstehen, wie unser Geschäft funktioniert und was unsere Führungskräfte und Teams erfolgreich macht.
 

Was dich bei VielfaltMenü erwartet
VielfaltMenü steht für „Mehr als gutes Essen.“
Wir versorgen täglich Menschen in Bildungseinrichtungen und entwickeln uns als Unternehmen kontinuierlich weiter. People & Culture soll dabei nicht nur verwalten, sondern die Entwicklung des Unternehmens aktiv unterstützen. Du bekommst deshalb die Möglichkeit, unser Recruiting nicht nur auszuführen, sondern mitzugestalten. Du arbeitest eng mit Führungskräften, dem People & Culture-Team sowie der Geschäftsführung zusammen und erhältst früh Verantwortung für eigene Recruitingprozesse. Gleichzeitig geben wir dir Raum, dich fachlich weiterzuentwickeln.
In deiner Rolle genießt du echten Gestaltungsspielraum: Du baust moderne Qualitäts- sowie Prozessstrukturen aktiv mit auf und prägst die Standards eines führenden Unternehmens für Kita- und Schulverpflegung in Deutschland. Dabei profitierst du von kurzen Entscheidungswegen und einer Geschäftsführung, die Qualität strategisch fördert.
Neben einem unbefristeten Arbeitsvertrag in einem zukunftssicheren Markt erwarten dich eine attraktive, transparente Vergütung sowie klare Entwicklungsperspektiven durch strukturierte Einarbeitung und individuelle Weiterbildungen. Wir unterstützen deine Work-Life-Balance durch 30 Urlaubstage, geregelte Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten. Zudem erhältst du moderne Arbeitsmittel inklusive Diensthandy. Eine gute ÖPNV-Anbindung und ein engagiertes, kollegiales Team runden unser Angebot ab.
 

Klingt nach dir?
Dann interessiert uns nicht nur dein Lebenslauf.
Wir möchten wissen, wie du über Menschen, Kompetenzen und gute Personalauswahl denkst.
Bewirb dich bei uns und gestalte gemeinsam mit uns, wie Recruiting bei VielfaltMenü künftig funktioniert.
 
VielfaltMenü – Mehr als gutes Essen.

title: Senior Frontend Engineer - React

We provide scientists with the help and support they need by connecting them to the world’s most active scientific community.

We've built a platform that gives the world's scientists the tools and services they need to connect, collaborate, and advance their research. Over 25 million members from 193 countries use ResearchGate to share, discover, and discuss research.


Objective of the role

We're looking for an enthusiastic frontend engineer with the skills and ability to turn great ideas into reality. You should have an in-depth understanding of current web technologies and front-end development, and be passionate about creating a great user experience. Your input will help us grow and maintain our React front-end.

You will be an integral part of the product team dedicated to enhancing ResearchGate's publisher-facing product. This role involves designing, constructing, and refining the platform to further our mission of facilitating global scientific connections and ensuring open access to research. At present, our team is working on making ResearchGate a great platform for publishers to connect with existing and future authors.

Your immediate colleagues will consist of JavaScript and PHP engineers, an Engineering Manager, a Product Manager, a UX Designer, and a UX Writer. Our team places great value on our collaborative and communicative work culture and we eagerly anticipate integrating a new Engineer into this environment.

  • Create web interfaces using TypeScript and React for new products and features.

  • Collaborate with Product Managers, Designers, and Software Engineers to deliver compelling publisher-facing products.

  • You take responsibility over your own solutions and continuously improve them.

SAP S/4HANA Fachbereichskoordinator (m/w/d)

Über uns

Wir sehen die Halbleiterindustrie als Raum voller Möglichkeiten. Wir sehen Chancen. Und wir sehen das enorme Potenzial unserer Graphenlösungen, die Branche grundlegend zu verändern. Wir laden dich ein, diesen Wandel mitzugestalten und mit unserem konsequent menschenorientierten Ansatz kluge Köpfe für eine gemeinsame Vision zu vereinen.

Unsere Vision: Zeige allen, dass du grundlegende Veränderungen bewirken kannst. Beweise mit deinem Wissen und deinen Fähigkeiten, dass Dinge auch anders gemacht werden können. Gemeinsam verändern wir die Art und Weise, wie die Welt miteinander verbunden ist.

Über unsere Technologie

Die Halbleiterindustrie benötigt zunehmend leistungsfähigere Chips mit höherer Bandbreite und geringerem Energieverbrauch. Unsere Technologie bietet dafür eine Lösung: Wir verbinden Chips zu leistungsstarken Computernetzwerken mit hohem Datendurchsatz und geringer Latenz.

Der Schlüssel liegt in den besonderen physikalischen Eigenschaften von Graphen. Sie ermöglichen es uns, elektronische Datenverarbeitung mit photonischer Kommunikation zu verbinden, sodass unzählige Chips nahezu so miteinander interagieren können, als wären sie ein einziger. Unsere Innovation im Bereich der Graphenphotonik hebt Rechenleistung und Energieeffizienz auf ein völlig neues Niveau.

Kurz gesagt: Wir verbinden Chips zu leistungsstarken und energieeffizienten Netzwerken und überwinden damit bestehende Grenzen der Konnektivität in der Halbleiterindustrie. Wir liefern die Graphenlösung.

Deine Rolle

Die Black Semiconductor GmbH sucht einen SAP S/4HANA Fachbereichskoordinator (m/w/d), der als zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen den Fachbereichen und externen SAP-Beratern agiert und sicherstellt, dass geschäftliche Anforderungen effektiv in geeignete Systemlösungen übersetzt werden.

Du betreust und pflegst unsere SAP S/4HANA Systemlandschaft über die Bereiche Finance, Logistik, Einkauf und Supply Chain hinweg. Dabei treibst du die kontinuierliche Verbesserung von Geschäftsprozessen, die Optimierung des Systems und die erfolgreiche Umsetzung von Änderungen voran.

Deine Verantwortlichkeiten

  • Zentrale Ansprechperson für die Fachbereiche Finance, Logistik, Einkauf und Supply Chain sowie für externe SAP-Beratungspartner

title: Senior Producer
description:
Senior Producer

ScapeWorld Entertainment

Remote. Our working day runs on CET, wherever you sit. Full time, on a long-term contract. Starting as soon as you can. Where you live while you do is up to you; the location field on this posting only fits one country, so please read this as the real rule and apply from wherever you are.

About us

We are Scape, a Swedish game studio of about 30 people, fully remote by choice. We are launching Scape on Steam Early Access later this year: a growing platform of multiplayer games where a player's identity carries across all of them. The first game inside Scape is Gravity: a precision climbing game where 100 players share one server, one tower, and one long way down. Our senior team has shipped and run live games at studios including Arrowhead (Helldivers 2), Avalanche Studios, Epic and Ubisoft.

Since we are a small team about to put our first game in front of players, we are looking for the person who holds the plan, the priorities and the team together while we do it. If that sounds like you, we would love to meet.

The role

Let us start with the studio you would be joining. Around thirty people, fully remote, and a group of strong leads in design, art, engineering, QA, community and commercial who own their crafts and run their own teams. What we do not have is the person who looks across all of them at once, holds the plan they are all working to, and makes the day-to-day calls that keep it moving as one. That is this role. It is the only production seat in the company, and it comes with real authority.

You would work closely with the Creative Director. They own what the game is, set the direction and make the big bets. You own the plan that gets us there and the decisions inside it: scope, sequencing and trade-offs within a milestone are yours to make, and you decide which questions need to reach them and which do not. They should be able to step back and know that things are being handled, because they are.

In practice, it comes down to four things:

You know how a game gets made. You can see what depends on what, where the effort really sits, and whether an estimate is going to hold. When a lead tells you how long something takes, you know how to hear it and what has to land for the work to ship on time.

You own the plan and the priorities. Not just the schedule, but the order of work behind it. When two things compete, you decide, or you get the decision made and tell everyone affected. Open questions have an owner and a date. Nothing sits unanswered because nobody was sure whose call it was.

You plan ahead. Problems get found while they are still cheap, and everything that has to land together lands together: builds, assets, store material, localization, press dates.

You lead the team's delivery. People know the plan is real, feel good about hitting it, and are still standing when it ships. The leads lead their crafts. You lead how it all comes together, and you meet each team where it is: some want you in the weeds with them on estimates and sequencing, others mainly need the picture across teams kept current. You read which is which.

We have a production pipeline that works, and like any pipeline it can always be better. You would inherit it as it is, get to know it and the people who run it, and then improve it where you see the need. Nobody here expects you to arrive with all the answers. We do hope you arrive curious about how we work and comfortable telling us, kindly and clearly, where we could do better.


What you will own

  • Production priorities day to day: the order of work across the studio, the trade-off calls within a milestone, and every open question that is blocking someone. You find who can answer, get it answered or escalated with a clear recommendation attached, and close the loop with the teams waiting on it. If a question is blocking someone, it is yours until it is not

  • Keeping design, art, engineering, QA and marketing in step with each other, week by week, so nobody is working against a version of the plan that has moved

  • The forward view: every feature in flight, what each one is still waiting on, the handoffs between departments caught early, and risk seen while it is still cheap, named, and carrying a mitigation before it turns into a schedule event

  • The team's delivery health: sustainable pace, morale, and delivery on target, treated as one problem rather than a trade-off

  • Marketing as a real production dependency, and the alignment dates around release: builds, assets, store material, localization drops, press dates, landing on time and together

  • The production plan behind all of it: a milestone schedule with a baseline, a forecast per milestone from velocity against remaining scope, estimates held against actuals, and replanning on a cycle rather than after something breaks

  • QA in step with everyone else. Our QA lead owns testing; you make sure QA knows what is coming and when, that testable builds land when the plan says they do, and that the QA window sits in the schedule where it belongs rather than where it ends up

  • External production partners: localization, video, 3D, anything we outsource. You own the relationship and the communication in both directions, and you chase. Briefs and context going out, deliveries coming in and landing in the build, and the schedule that keeps them in step with everyone else. Leads should never have to chase a partner themselves. The craft stays with the partner; making it fit is on you

  • The production process itself and the tools it runs through. We use Jira, including Jira Plans for planning months out against a baseline, and you own it for the studio. You also support hiring managers through their recruitment processes, so a lead who is hiring can focus on assessing the person rather than running the process


You

Most people who can do this job have around five years in games production behind them. Take that as a description of who tends to apply, not a bar we hold. If you can show us the things below with less, please apply anyway. We would rather meet you than miss you.

  • You know how games get made across disciplines: what waits on what, how long things really take, and where a plan is optimistic before the dates say so

  • You have produced across several titles and taken at least one PC title all the way to release, including the closing stretch: feature lock, bug burn, submission, the go decision. Which store matters less than that you have been through a PC launch. Projects that were cancelled along the way still count; we know how the last few years have gone for a lot of good people

  • You have owned priorities, not just a schedule. You have made cut-or-keep calls on a shipped title and lived with them, and you can tell us about one you got wrong

  • You have worked closely with a founder, studio head or creative director, and you know how to take decisions off their plate without going around them

  • You have built and driven a schedule, and you have written down a way of working that other people picked up and used. We would love to see examples, in whatever form they exist

  • You have led a team to a target without burning it out, and the people on it would work with you again

  • You are proactive by default and you work independently. You do not wait to be asked or chased; given an assignment, you find out what it needs and finish it well without someone checking each step. That is what senior means to us

  • Leads tell you how things are really going, because you talk with them directly and they trust you with the real picture

  • You are fluent in Jira at the level of owning it for a team, Jira Plans included. It is a tool, not the job, but it is the tool we run the plan through, so we need you good with it

  • You work our day, which runs on CET; where you sit while you do is up to you. And you are comfortable working in English, written and spoken


Helpful, not required

  • Steam specifically: Steamworks, builds and depots, the store page, review and submission, and how Early Access behaves through the whole run

  • Live operations and a patch cadence

  • Working with external production partners before, on either side of the relationship

  • Time at a small studio where you were the only producer, or where the producer and product owner were the same person

  • A remote-first team


What we offer

The whole project and the authority that comes with it. Real decisions, not just a schedule to report against. Strong leads beside you rather than under you, and a Creative Director who wants to hand things over and means it. A company small enough that what you do is visible in what we ship, and people who will notice.

We are a self-motivated team, remote by choice and flexible in how we work, and we run on people helping each other rather than watching each other. Everyone here is trusted to own their part and supported when they need a hand, and we would like that to be true for you from your first week.

And we are early. Scape is heading to Steam with everything still ahead of it. Joining now means building something with a real chance of becoming big, and being one of the people it belongs to when it does.


Practical

  • Remote. Our working day runs on CET and this role keeps it.

  • Full time, on a long-term contract.

  • Start: as soon as you can. Tell us your notice period in the application form and we will work around it.

  • Recruitment is ongoing.

title: Remote Maintenance Engineer
description:
About the role

Gauss Fusion is aiming to build the first commercial scale fusion power plant based on the stellarator concept and is seeking an experienced mechanical engineer to lead on development of the robotic maintenance approach.
The fusion environment within the reactor is very aggressive, and in-vessel components such as the breeder blanket and divertor will need to be replaced on a regular basis as the materials become damaged by the radiation. Due to the environment inside the device, and in order to maintain a high overall availability, the maintenance must be done robotically using automated systems to extract and replace the components and bring the removed ones to a hot cell for separation, waste treatment, and recycling.
Gauss Fusion is looking for an innovative mechanical design engineer with experience in robotics to lead the work defining and developing the maintenance approach for the Gauss stellarator power plant and its key stellarator systems. While the magnetic configuration will be designed to maximise access to the reactor, the complex geometry poses a challenge to fixations and kinematics, and inventive approaches to the problem are required.


Main responsibilities

Manage the Gauss Fusion maintenance approach to meet the requirements of a commercial scale fusion power plant design:

  • Develop workable approaches to achieving high power plant availability, taking account of engineering and physics requirements across the reactor.
  • Integrate these remote maintenance requirements into plant layout specifications.
  • Define approaches to minimising hot cell inventory through efficient handling of removed components.
  • Lead development of the breeder blanket and divertor segmentation and fixations resulting from these approaches.
  • Lead development of remote maintenance testing and demonstration systems for the reactor.


Qualification and educational requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or related field, master’s or Ph.D. preferred.
  • Technical experience: 
    • Minimum of 6 years of experience in mechanical engineering, preferably in large-scale engineering projects.
    • Experience in designing complex mechanical systems, preferably in the energy or nuclear industry.
    • Familiarity with CAD software and engineering analysis tools.


Competences and preferred skills

  • Experience developing remote maintenance systems operating in hazardous environments
  • Strong background in mechatronics, motion control and mechanical integration. 
  • Experience with digital mock-up will be an asset
  • Familiarity with maintenance, inspection and intervention systems 
  • Familiarity with system engineering processes, requirements management and verification activities. Strong understanding of mechanical design principles and engineering mechanics.
  • Proficiency in structural analysis, finite element analysis (FEA), and kinematic analysis.

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to shape some of the most important experiences in our marketplace. You'll own complex, high-impact problem spaces end to end, from ambiguous discovery through to shipped, measured outcomes and raise the bar for design craft and pace across the whole team.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with real influence. You'll partner directly with product and engineering leadership, mentor other designers, and set the standard for how design work gets done at Carwow.

A note on how we work: AI fluency is integral to the role. Our design team works AI-natively. We use Claude Design (and similar tools) to move from idea to high-quality prototype in hours, not weeks, and we expect designers at this level to be genuinely fluent in this way of working, not just curious about it. If you're still designing the way teams did in 2023, this probably isn't the right role. If you've rebuilt your workflow around AI and it's made you dramatically faster and more ambitious, we'd love to talk.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • Own end-to-end design for a major problem space in our marketplace. Buying, selling, or dealer-facing products. from discovery and framing through to launch and iteration

  • Prototype at pace using AI design tools (Claude Design or equivalent), getting real, testable experiences in front of users and stakeholders early and often

  • Work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers, using AI-assisted workflows to close the gap between design intent and shipped product, ideally getting hands-on in code where it speeds things up

  • Set direction, not just execute: identify opportunities, make the case with evidence, and bring product and engineering partners with you

  • Raise the craft bar across the team through critique, mentorship, and by making your own work an example worth following

  • Champion AI-native ways of working. Sharing techniques, building reusable prompts and workflows, and helping the wider team level up

  • Ground decisions in evidence, combining user research, data, and rapid experimentation

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

  • 7+ years of product design experience, with a track record of leading complex, high-impact work in consumer or marketplace products

  • A high degree of AI fluency. Hands-on, demonstrable experience using Claude Design (or an equivalent AI design/prototyping tool) as a core part of your workflow. This is critical to the role, and we'll want to see it in your portfolio and hear about it in interviews

  • Strong end-to-end craft: you can go from a fuzzy problem statement to polished, production-ready design, and everything you ship is considered

  • Comfort with ambiguity and pace. You make good decisions with incomplete information and iterate quickly

  • Excellent communication and influence: you can align senior stakeholders, tell a compelling story with your work, and hold your ground constructively

  • Experience mentoring designers and lifting the standard of a team|

STRONGLY PREFERRED SKILLS

  • Experience with Claude Code (or an equivalent AI coding agent) — enough to prototype in real code, collaborate more deeply with engineers, or ship small changes yourself

  • Marketplace, e-commerce, or two-sided platform experience

  • Familiarity with experimentation-driven product development (A/B testing, funnel analysis)

 

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first six months you'll have taken ownership of a significant problem space, shipped work that measurably moves a core metric, and become someone other designers seek out — both for the quality of your craft and for how you use AI tools to work at a pace and ambition level others want to copy.


WHY CARWOW?

  • Genuine scale and impact: your work is used by millions of car buyers and sellers

  • An AI-forward culture where new tools and workflows are embraced, not resisted — with access to the best tooling available

  • A senior, supportive design team that takes craft seriously

  • Hybrid working, competitive salary and equity, private healthcare, enhanced parental leave, and a car-buying perk you'd expect from us

HOW TO APPLY

  • Send us your CV and portfolio. Please include at least one example of work where AI tools (Claude Design, Claude Code, or equivalents) played a meaningful role in your process — tell us what you used, how, and what it changed about the outcome.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our award-winning Data Science team at a pivotal moment. Carwow operates a two-sided marketplace — connecting car buyers and sellers at scale — and data science sits at the heart of how we make that marketplace smarter, faster, and more valuable for everyone in it. In fact, we recently won GenAI initiative of the Year at the British Data Awards.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role working centrally across the business. You'll partner with teams spanning Commercial, Marketing, Product, Finance, Engineering and Operations — developing and deploying ML and AI solutions that drive outcomes across both sides of our marketplace. The problems you'll work on are genuinely varied: pricing models, propensity and demand signals that sharpen marketing spend, personalised recommendations for our web product and CRM, and LLM-powered solutions for operational challenges like document verification.

You'll translate ambiguous business problems into structured, production-ready solutions — and you'll be expected to deliver them end-to-end, from first principles through to being deployment-ready and beyond.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • End-to-End ML & AI Delivery: Lead data science initiatives from problem framing through to deployment, monitoring, and iteration — delivering the full production lifecycle.   • GenAI & LLM Application: Design and build LLM-powered solutions where they create genuine business value — document processing, intelligent search, content understanding, and beyond. Apply them alongside classical ML with clear judgement about where each approach earns its place.

  • Commercial Impact: Connect your work directly to business outcomes. Whether you're building a model to improve marketing efficiency, a pricing signal to sharpen commercial decisions, or a recommendation engine to increase conversion — you understand the business lever you're pulling and design your solutions accordingly.

  • Sound Judgement: You navigate the tooling landscape with clear eyes — knowing when classical ML is right, when GenAI unlocks something new, and when a simpler solution is the more honest answer. Strong instincts for scalability, reliability, and explainability.

title: Design Engineer
description:
About Aibidia

Aibidia is a fast-growing SaaS company transforming how multinational businesses manage transfer pricing. We're building intelligent, scalable software that simplifies complex tax and compliance processes, helping some of the world's largest organisations work more efficiently and confidently.

We're a team that values curiosity, ownership and pragmatic problem-solving. As we continue to evolve our products and embrace AI-native ways of working, we're looking for a Design Engineer to help shape the next generation of our platform.

The Role

We're looking for an AI-first Design Engineer who combines strong technical capabilities with a solid understanding of product design, UX and usability.

This is a hybrid role at the intersection of design and engineering. You'll work on complex, data-rich enterprise software, using modern AI tools to rapidly prototype, iterate and deliver intuitive product experiences.

We're not looking for someone who simply creates beautiful interfaces or follows traditional, lengthy design processes. We want someone who thinks systematically, understands how software is built and knows how to leverage AI to turn complex requirements into functional, user-friendly solutions.

You'll join a team that has already established an AI-first design system and modern ways of working. Rather than reinventing what's already in place, you'll build on these foundations, contributing to an evolving design system while helping us move towards faster, more iterative product development.

What You'll Do

Design, prototype and ship

  • Translate complex business requirements and user needs into intuitive, functional product experiences.

  • Rapidly prototype and iterate on new features using AI-powered tools, getting working solutions in front of users early.

  • Work closely with Product Managers, Engineers and domain experts to take ideas from concept through to implementation.

  • Balance usability, technical feasibility and speed of delivery, knowing when to iterate and when a solution is good enough to ship.

  • Design for complex, data-heavy workflows where clarity, efficiency and accuracy matter more than visual embellishment.

Build with an AI-first mindset

  • Use AI tools such as Claude, Figma and MCP integrations as a core part of your design and development workflow.

  • Experiment with emerging AI technologies, agents and workflows to continuously improve how we build products.

  • Apply sound design and engineering judgement to AI-generated outputs, ensuring quality, usability and consistency.

Contribute to our design system

  • Build on and contribute to our existing AI-first design system, ensuring consistency and scalability across the product.

  • Understand and apply design system principles, including components, design tokens, spacing, layouts, accessibility and interaction patterns.

  • Identify opportunities to improve components, documentation and AI-assisted design workflows.

Collaborate and validate

  • Work directly with users and internal stakeholders to understand problems, validate ideas and gather feedback.

  • Take a lean, iterative approach to product development, prioritising early validation over lengthy discovery cycles.

  • Collaborate closely with Engineering to ensure designs are technically achievable and can be efficiently implemented.

  • Continuously refine solutions based on user feedback, technical constraints and evolving business needs.

What We're Looking For

  • A hybrid design and engineering background, with hands-on coding capabilities and a strong understanding of UX, UI and usability principles.

  • Experience using modern AI tools as an integral part of your workflow, with a genuine interest in AI-assisted design, prototyping and development.

  • Strong systems thinking, with an understanding of how scalable design systems, reusable components and technical frameworks work together.

  • Experience contributing to design systems, with knowledge of design tokens, component libraries, accessibility and established UI patterns.

  • Experience working directly with codebases, GitHub and modern frontend technologies, rather than operating solely within traditional design tools.

  • Experience designing or building complex, data-dense B2B SaaS, enterprise or workflow-driven products.

  • Experience working in a startup or scaleup environment, where priorities evolve, teams are lean and speed of execution matters.

  • Strong product judgement and the ability to balance user needs, business requirements and technical constraints.

  • A curious, adaptable mindset and enthusiasm for experimenting with emerging technologies and new ways of working.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in fintech, tax technology, compliance or other complex, regulated industries.

  • Exposure to both early-stage startups and larger, more established software organisations.


Why Join Aibidia?

  • Build the future of AI-first product development: Help shape how AI is embedded into the way we design, prototype and ship software.

  • Solve genuinely complex problems: Work on sophisticated enterprise software where thoughtful design and usability have a meaningful impact.

  • Make an impact: Join a lean, collaborative team where your ideas, technical judgement and contributions directly influence the product.

  • Work with modern tools: Experiment with emerging AI technologies and continuously improve how products are built.

  • Grow with us: Be part of a scaling international SaaS business that's challenging traditional approaches to tax technology.

Benefits & Perks:

  • 💰 Share in Aibidia’s success – Enjoy a competitive compensation and incentive package that rewards your contribution.

  • 🏡 Flexible, hybrid working – Flexible working hours and a hybrid policy designed to support how you work best.

  • 🩺 Comprehensive healthcare – A healthcare package to support you and your wellbeing.

  • 💚 Wellbeing that matters – A genuine focus on physical and mental wellbeing, supported by our internal Health & Wellbeing Committee.

  • 🎉 Time to celebrate together – Regular team socials, including our much-loved summer and winter parties.

  • 💻 The best tools for the job – Access to the latest technology to help you do your best work.

  • 🚀 Invest in your growth – Performance-based development is part of our culture, with a dedicated learning budget for every employee.

  • 🌍 Make an impact globally – Join a fast-growing global SaaS company using technology to transform a traditionally complex industry.

  • 🤝 Low hierarchy, high collaboration – Work in an open, collaborative environment where ideas are valued and everyone has the opportunity to make an impact.

 

We are committed to fostering an inclusive culture that celebrates diversity, we want you to bring you, no matter your background, gender, race or sexual orientation!

Please note, we’re unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role. To be considered, you’ll need to show proof of your eligibility to work in the country.

title: Post-doctorant.e : "Simulation numérique 3D de l’infusion de composites à fibres naturelles" - CDD 12 mois
description:
ENGLISH VERSION

Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !

Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.

🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vous

Ce post-doctorat s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet ANR PRME LINEN (Experimental and Numerical Characterisation of Flax Composite Manufacturing by Liquid Infusion: From Local Phenomena to Induced Properties), auquel participent plusieurs chercheurs de l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne, avec pour objectif d’étudier l’élaboration de pièces structurales en matériaux composites à base de fibres de lin.

Ce post-doctorat, d’une durée de 12 mois est proposé pour développer la modélisation numérique de l’infusion de résine dans des préformes composites à fibres de lin. L’objectif est d’étudier, à l’échelle mésoscopique, l’influence de l’organisation anisotrope et hétérogène des torons de fibres sur l’écoulement de la résine. Le projet s’appuiera sur des simulations 3D par éléments finis, reposant sur un couplage Stokes-Darcy et la prise en compte d’un tenseur de perméabilité orthotrope. Une attention particulière sera portée à l’influence des variations locales de la fraction volumique de fibres sur la perméabilité, les chemins préférentiels d’écoulement et les effets capillaires. Les simulations seront réalisées avec le code éléments finis Cœur (https://gitlab.emse.fr/bruchon/Coeur), en s’appuyant sur la bibliothèque PETSc et des solveurs itératifs préconditionnés adaptés aux problèmes de grande taille. Dans un premier temps, des architectures idéalisées de type unidirectionnel, quasi-unidirectionnel et tissé seront étudiées à l’aide d’une représentation par Level-Set. Dans un second temps, lorsque cela sera possible, des mésostructures réalistes seront reconstruites à partir d’images µ-CT.

Le post-doctorant.e contribuera également au développement et à la validation de la stratégie numérique et travaillera en interaction étroite avec les travaux expérimentaux et numériques des autres tâches du projet.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Une formation en mécanique numérique, mécanique des fluides, éléments finis ou calcul scientifique est recherchée.

Des compétences en C++/Python, calcul haute performance, PETSc, méthodes Level-Set ou traitement d’images 3D seront appréciées.

· Capacité à travailler en équipe

Cross-functionele verbeterprojecten die over meerdere teams heen lopen, leid je in principe zelf.

Dat vraagt senioriteit. Je moet een Head kunnen challengen wanneer de customer experience niet goed genoeg is, maar net zo makkelijk zelf een review beantwoorden, een geautomatiseerde e-mail herschrijven of een (kleiner) verbeterproject van A tot Z uitvoeren.

  • Cross-functionele CX-projecten die over meerdere teams heen lopen, leid je in principe zelf van analyse tot implementatie.

  • Je meet na implementatie of verbeteringen daadwerkelijk het gewenste effect op de customer experience hebben gehad.

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor onze aanpak rondom Google Reviews en Trustpilot: je zorgt dat reviews snel en goed worden beantwoord, dat problemen bij de juiste eigenaar terechtkomen en dat noodzakelijke opvolging snel plaatsvindt.

Hoe ziet succes eruit?

Makkelijk van het gas af. Dat moet de ervaring van onze klanten zijn gedurende de hele customer journey. Na de belangrijkste onderdelen van deze journey vragen we onze klanten actief om feedback. De scores op deze customer feedback vormen belangrijke KPI’s voor deze rol en laten zien waar de ervaring goed is en waar deze beter moet.

Onze Google- en Trustpilot-scores zijn belangrijke overkoepelende KPI’s voor de totale customer experience. Het doel is daarbij niet alleen om scores te verbeteren, maar vooral om de onderliggende customer experience structureel beter te maken.

Daarom kijken we ook naar hoe snel en goed customer feedback en reviews worden opgevolgd, hoeveel structurele customer pain points we oplossen en hoe snel en met welke kwaliteit de belangrijkste CX-improvement projecten worden gerealiseerd.

We zoeken iemand die continu ziet hoe het beter kan en vervolgens zorgt dat het ook beter wordt. Je combineert een hoge kwaliteitsstandaard en sterk analytisch vermogen met executiekracht. Je kunt diep de details induiken, maar ook bepalen waar de grootste impact ligt en op senior niveau door de hele organisatie verbeteringen realiseren.

Ook wanneer klanten tevreden zijn en duidelijke feedback opdroogt, blijf je zoeken naar hoe de customer experience nog beter kan.

title: Lead Controls & Data Engineer
description:
At DeWarmte, we develop technology that helps homes move away from gas. Our heat pumps combine hardware, embedded control software, cloud services and data—and the quality of the software connecting those elements directly determines how well our products perform in customers’ homes.


We are looking for a Lead Controls & Data Engineer to take ownership of two foundations of our products: the control software that operates our heat pumps and the data platform that helps us monitor, understand and improve them.


This is a hands-on leadership role. Initially, most of your time will be spent writing code, diagnosing real-world behaviour, improving reliability and delivering new functionality. At the same time, you are in the lead for collaborating with external partners, ensuring data reliability and scalability. Additionally, you will build the technical foundations, documentation and team that move us away from dependence on any one engineer.

Your mission

Build reliable, scalable controls and data capability that is owned by a team—not an individual.

You will inherit working systems and products already operating in the field. Your job is to understand them deeply, keep them running, improve their performance and evolve their architecture. You will then recruit and develop the engineers needed to create durable, shared ownership.

What you'll do

Own and improve our control software

  • Work directly in the production code that controls our heat pumps.

  • Design, build, test and deploy new control functionality.

  • Improve product performance, stability, safety and energy efficiency.

  • Diagnose and understand complex behaviour across software, electronics, sensors, hydraulics and the physical installation.

  • Manage controlled software rollouts across both new products and the installed fleet.

  • Establish appropriate automated testing, simulation, observability and release practices.

  • Current stack includes Bash/Shell, Python, Kafka, Telegraf and Influx. You will own the evolution of the stack together with our Hardware R&D team.


Build our product data platform

  • Take technical ownership of the systems that collect, process and expose data from our connected smart heat pumps.

  • Make product behaviour and fleet trends observable for engineering, service and product teams.

  • Improve the quality, reliability and accessibility of operational data.

  • Ensure pipeline and server capabilities are able to handle rapid scaling.

  • Create the foundations for performance analysis, remote diagnostics and continuous product improvement.

  • Define clear interfaces between device software, cloud systems, the customer app and internal tools.


Build a team and eliminate key-person dependency

  • Turn implicit knowledge into clear documentation, tooling and repeatable engineering practices.

  • Design systems that other engineers can intuitively understand, easily test and safely change.

  • Define the roles and capabilities the team will need as DeWarmte scales.

  • Recruit, onboard and mentor controls, embedded-software and data engineers.

  • Introduce effective code reviews, technical decision-making and shared operational ownership.

  • Gradually move from being the primary implementer to leading a capable team—without losing touch with the code.


Work across the product

You will collaborate closely with colleagues in hardware, software, data, product development, assembly, installation and service. You will help resolve immediate customer and operational issues while protecting the long-term quality of the platform.

 

What success looks like

In your first months

  • You understand the existing controls, data flows and operational risks.

  • You can independently maintain, debug and release the current systems.

  • The most important technical risks and knowledge gaps are visible and prioritised.

  • Monitoring, documentation and development practices begin to improve.


As the role develops

  • New control functionality can be delivered predictably and safely.

  • You work closely together with Hardware colleagues, developing the next generation of products

  • Product data supports faster diagnosis and better engineering decisions.

  • Critical systems are understood and maintained by more than one person.

  • A small, strong controls and data team is in place, with clear ownership and effective ways of working.

  • DeWarmte is no longer dependent on a single engineer to operate or evolve this part of the product.

What we are looking for

  • Strong hands-on software engineering experience, including ownership of production systems.

  • Experience developing control or embedded software for physical products, machines or connected devices.

  • A track record of taking functionality through design, implementation, testing, deployment and real-world operation.

  • The ability to reason across software, hardware and physical-system behaviour.

  • Experience working with telemetry, time-series data, data pipelines or connected-device platforms.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals, including version control, automated testing, CI/CD, observability and structured incident resolution.

  • The ability to create clarity in an environment where systems and processes are still developing.

  • Experience mentoring engineers and improving how a team works.

  • The ambition and ability to recruit and lead a team while remaining highly hands-on.


Experience with heat pumps, HVAC systems, safety-critical design, fleet-management systems or optimisation is valuable, but we care more about your ability to learn a complex physical product and take genuine end-to-end ownership.

How you work

  • You solve urgent problems without allowing permanent workarounds to become the architecture.

  • You explain complex technical matters clearly to people with different backgrounds.

  • You balance reliability today with the investments needed to scale tomorrow.

Geen koude acquisitie dus. Nooit.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure
description:
Staff Software Engineer, Platform & Infrastructure

The role

We are hiring a Staff Software Engineer for our Infrastructure team.

Stream runs behind apps that more than a billion people use: billions of API requests a month, a 99.999% uptime promise, and a small team keeping it all running. Infrastructure here decides how fast our products feel, how well they scale, and how quickly we can launch new ones.

This year we're wrapping up a big move. We're simplifying where and how we host, and rebuilding our data layer on self-hosted, open-source systems that are faster and cheaper to run. That's the groundwork, not the job. Next comes building the infrastructure every Stream product runs on, including the ones we haven't built yet. That means real SLOs, clear costs, calmer on-call, and a platform that helps teams ship faster.

What you build will shape how much Stream spends and how fast it grows, and we'll trust you with big decisions from your first few weeks.

This is a Software Engineering role first. Attitude, ambition and a willingness to experiment across the stack matter more to us than years of Kubernetes or database operations. We expect AI to cover a good share of the DevOps-heavy work, and we expect you to use it that way. What a tool can't give us is system design judgement, strong fundamentals and good code, so that is what we look for.

Platform & Infrastructure is a small, senior team without the support structures of a large organisation. It moves fast and it gets hectic. We would rather say that now than have you find out in month two.

 

What team is focusing on:

  • Runs Stream's global platform. Keeps the edge and backend that serve customers worldwide fast and up, at single-digit millisecond latency on a 99.999% uptime SLA.

  • Shapes Stream's margins. Our hosting and infrastructure decisions directly drive the company's profitability. You will decide where and how we run, and what we stop paying for.

  • Builds tools people actually want to use. Internal tools that change how engineers deploy and debug, and external ones that give customers a clear view of their own traffic and health.

  • Makes on-call boring. Builds a rotation people can sustain, and cuts alert noise until a page means something real is broken.

  • Makes cost visible. Gives every team a clear view of what it spends on infrastructure and why, so cost becomes part of every engineering decision.

What you will do:

  • Define what "good" looks like for the platform. Set latency and uptime SLOs for every product team, and decide what we measure, from error rates and delivery times to how healthy our customers' apps really are.

  • Make the big infrastructure calls. Lead the design reviews and decisions on where and how we run, working with backend, video and moderation engineers on tradeoffs that cross service boundaries.

  • Build the platform tooling. Write the internal tools and services that help engineers ship, deploy and debug faster, plus the docs and AI skills that make launching a new product repeatable.

  • Turn incidents into fixes that stick. Take part in on-call, and make sure every root cause ends in a durable fix, not a workaround.

  • Make cost part of every design. Weigh cost alongside reliability in every decision, and give teams the numbers to do the same.

What we are looking for:

  • A software engineer who has built systems, not only configured them. You write production code in Go, Python or a similar language. Scripting-only backgrounds are not a fit.

  • Strong system design. You can reason about failure modes, capacity and cost in distributed systems, and explain why you chose what you chose.

  • Solid fundamentals in networking, storage and concurrency, and the habit of asking why a system behaves the way it does instead of accepting the default.

  • You have owned high-scale production systems and set technical direction beyond your own work, through design reviews, RFCs and decisions other engineers build on.

  • You experiment. When you hit Kubernetes, a database or a cloud service you have not run before, you dig in, use AI to close the gap, and ship.

  • You already use AI tools every day in your engineering work.

  • You treat cost and reliability as engineering problems, and you can put a number on an outcome you drove.

  • You write clearly. Much of this role is docs and standards that other teams will follow.

  • You are comfortable in a small team, setting direction and reviewing a PR in the same week.

Nice to have experience:

  • Kubernetes in production: cluster architecture, workload design or a migration you led.

  • PostgreSQL at scale, ideally self-hosted or with CloudNativePG: sharding, replication, partitioning tradeoffs.

  • Valkey or Redis at scale, ideally on Kubernetes.

  • Hands-on AWS and GCP, including multi-cloud setups or migrations between providers.

  • Cloud commitment and reservation strategy (committed use discounts, savings plans), or formal FinOps practice.

  • SLO design, alert hygiene and a Prometheus and Grafana based observability stack.

  • Real-time systems: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming or other persistent-connection workloads.

  • Open source contributions, or writing and talks on cloud, platform or distributed systems.

Our stack

  • Go, gRPC, RocksDB, Python

  • PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ

  • GCP

  • Grafana, Prometheus, ELK (Elasticsearch and Kibana)

  • Jaeger and Tempo for distributed tracing, Datadog

  • Redis, Memcached

  • Claude Code, Cursor

You will thrive here if

  • You want platform and infrastructure problems at a scale most engineers never touch, and the autonomy to set the direction yourself.

  • You would rather try something, measure it and change course than wait for a perfect plan.

  • You ship fast and learn fast, including when it is hectic.

  • You are self-directed and comfortable working with a globally distributed team across time zones.

You probably will not if

  • You want to stay a specialist in one layer of the stack.

  • You want tightly scoped tickets and step-by-step direction.

  • You need a calm, highly predictable environment.

Compensation and benefits

For employees based in the Netherlands:

  • 28 days paid time off plus Dutch public holidays

  • Pension plan

  • Commute covered: an NS Business Card or a company Swapfiets

  • Fitness contribution of up to €60 a month toward a gym or sports club membership

  • Learning and development budget

  • Work from anywhere: up to four weeks a year

  • Full Dutch statutory leave, with Stream topping up paternity leave to 100% pay

  • Catered team lunches in the office, and snacks

  • MacBook Pro and peripherals

  • Relocation support, visa sponsorship and 30% ruling support

  • An office in the centre of Amsterdam

  • Conferences and meetups, as an attendee or a speaker

  • The chance to work on our open source SDKs

Why join Stream?

We're a Series B company with global presence and a team of around 145 people from more than 35 countries.

We're backed by Felicis Ventures, GGV Capital, 01 Advisors, Techstars, and Arthur Ventures, with angels including Dick Costolo (ex-CEO of Twitter), Olivier Pomel (CEO of Datadog), Tom Preston-Werner (co-founder of GitHub), and Nicolas Dessaigne (co-founder of Algolia).

We'll be straight with you: a startup is more demanding than a large company. There's no fixed playbook, you'll own things end to end, and you'll sometimes pick up work outside your title. That's also what makes it a fast place to grow. If you want real ownership and high scale more than structure and a set career ladder, you'll feel at home here.

title: VP, Growth
description:
About Nivoda

Nivoda is the operating system for the global jewellery industry. Our B2B marketplace connects jewellery retailers with diamond, gemstone and jewellery suppliers in 70+ countries, and we process $300M+ in annual transactions in a $350B industry that has barely been touched by technology.

We remove the traditional barriers of capital, geography and information asymmetry. An independent jeweller in Ohio can source from a cutter in Mumbai with the same ease, pricing and confidence as one of the world's largest chains. That's the whole point.

Our Mission 🚀

Diamond and gemstone trading has run on inefficiency, opacity and exclusivity for generations. Relationships were gatekept, pricing was hidden, and the size of your business decided the terms you got. We're building the infrastructure that changes that — so any jewellery business, anywhere, regardless of size, can compete on the quality of what they do rather than who they know.

The Marketing Team ⭐️

We're a remote-first, low-hierarchy company where the best idea wins. Marketing at Nivoda is at an inflection point: we have real product-market fit, thousands of businesses transacting, a category we have the opportunity to redefine, and a marketing function that has not yet been built to match the scale of the opportunity.

About the Role

We're hiring a VP of Growth to build Nivoda's marketing function from the ground up and turn it into a predictable growth engine for a two-sided global marketplace.

This is a builder's role, not a caretaker's or maintainer’s. You'll own the strategy, the growth model, the budget, the team and the number. You'll be the person who decides what Nivoda's category story is in partnership with the CEO, how we reach tens of thousands of independent jewellers and suppliers, and how we prove — with data, not decks — which of those bets are working.

You'll report directly to the President and sit on the senior leadership team, with a mandate that spans demand generation, product marketing, brand, content, lifecycle and marketing operations across every market we trade in.

What would you be doing?

  • Owning Nivoda's marketing strategy end to end - translating company goals into a growth model, then into the channels, programmes and headcount that deliver it

  • Building the marketing team from its current base: hiring, structuring and levelling up a global team, and building the systems, briefs and feedback loops that make good marketers great

  • Owning demand generation and pipeline contribution for both sides of the marketplace - retailers who need supply, and suppliers who need demand

  • Building the measurement layer: attribution, funnel instrumentation, CAC and payback by segment and geography, and a reporting rhythm the leadership team actually trusts

  • Running marketing as a portfolio of experiments rather than a calendar of campaigns - defining leading indicators, killing what doesn't work quickly, and going all-in on what does

  • Owning positioning and product marketing across a multi-product platform (diamonds, gemstones, melee, bridal, finished jewellery, payments and logistics) so each launch lands with the right segment

  • Building the category narrative for "the operating system for the jewellery industry" - and making Nivoda the default name in an industry that still runs on WhatsApp and trade shows

  • Driving lifecycle and retention marketing in partnership with Product: onboarding, activation, reactivation and share-of-wallet growth inside existing accounts

  • Partnering closely with Sales and Revenue leadership on segmentation, ICP definition, territory support and sales enablement - marketing that helps close, not just fill the top

  • Localising go-to-market across our biggest markets, from the US and UK to India, Europe and Asia, without fragmenting the brand

  • Owning the marketing budget and making a clear, defensible case for where every dollar goes and what it returned

  • Representing marketing at leadership and board level - bringing a point of view on where growth comes from next, and the evidence behind it

What do we need from you?

  • Significant experience leading marketing in B2B SMB - selling to owner-operators and small businesses, not enterprise procurement committees. You understand that a high-volume, lower-ACV motion is a fundamentally different sport

  • A track record of building marketing teams and functions from the ground up. You've been the first or second marketing leader, hired the team, chosen the stack and created the operating model. Maintaining someone else's machine is not what you're looking for

  • Deep, hands-on data and growth orientation. You build growth models, instrument funnels, run experiments with real statistical discipline, and can talk fluently about CAC, payback, conversion by stage and cohort behaviour. You're as comfortable in the numbers as you are in the narrative

  • Demonstrated ownership of a pipeline or revenue number, with the receipts — you can walk us through what you inherited, what you changed, and what it did to the funnel

  • Full-stack breadth: you've owned some combination of performance, content, product marketing, lifecycle and brand, and you know which of them matters most right now versus in eighteen months

  • Genuine senior leadership: you've hired, managed managers, made hard calls on people and priorities, and held your own with a founder, CEO or board

  • The judgement to say no. You can name the channels you deliberately didn't pursue and explain why, anchored to the company's go-to-market model

  • Comfort with ambiguity and low hierarchy. You're happy to write the ad copy yourself one week and present the three-year growth model the next

  • Excellent written and spoken English, and the ability to operate across time zones in a globally distributed team

Nice to have

  • Experience marketing a two-sided marketplace, where supply and demand have to be grown in step

  • Background in a traditional, offline-heavy industry going through digital transformation — jewellery, construction, logistics, food service, wholesale, agriculture

  • Experience in a company that scaled from roughly $10M to $100M+ in GMV or revenue

  • International go-to-market experience across multiple regions and languages

  • Familiarity with a modern growth stack — HubSpot, Mixpanel or similar product analytics, and a warehouse-backed reporting setup

We're collaborative, fast-moving and allergic to bureaucracy. We're growing exponentially, which means real ownership and real scope — the work you do here is visible, and it compounds. title: People Controlling and Analytics Manager (m/f/d)
description:
ABOUT US

Unzer is a leading European fintech company with a mission to simplify international payments for e-commerce and retail businesses. Our brand was formed from 13 companies that now contribute to building a unique product covering the entire payment flow.  

At Unzer, we are driven by the belief that customers should enjoy a seamless shopping experience, no matter where they choose to shop. We are a team of over 750 experts from 50+ different nationalities, dedicated to creating a state-of-the-art unified commerce platform. Our goal is to enable businesses to delight their customers with a seamless payment experience.  

Whether you're a tech enthusiast, a payment expert, or a dedicated support professional, we are looking for individuals who are passionate about making a difference.  

Our offices: We are based across Austria, Denmark, Germany, and Luxembourg with a HQ in Berlin.  

ABOUT THE TEAM

Do you want your work to create a real impact? Join our team and help take data-driven decision-making in workforce management to the next level. In this role, you will connect people data with financial metrics and transform them into valuable insights, forecasts, and recommendations for our stakeholders. 

You will work closely with Finance, People function, and other business functions to support strategic decisions related to workforce planning and efficiency improvement. With your analytical mindset and drive for continuous improvement, you will actively contribute to the development and optimization of processes, tools, and strategies. You can expect a dynamic, fast-paced environment with a high degree of ownership, where your ideas matter, and you can help shape change. 


What your work will look like:

  • Own the analysis of personnel cost and FTE variances, identifying drivers, risks, and opportunities, and translating findings into clear recommendations for action. 

  • Lead workforce planning, forecasting, and scenario modeling, translating operational developments into financial impacts and strategic recommendations. 

  • Support monthly and annual closing activities within the People function, ensuring methodological consistency and audit readiness. 

  • Develop and optimize dashboards, models, and KPI frameworks relating to headcount, personnel costs, hiring, and ad hoc analyses, while driving standardization and automation. 

  • Identify opportunities to improve existing processes and implement enhancements that increase speed, accuracy, and efficiency across analytics and controlling workflows. 

  • Collaborate closely with Payroll, Accounting, Controlling and Analytics teams to ensure high data quality, consistent KPIs, and reliable reporting. 


What you need to be successful in this role:

  • Proven experience in Controlling, Analytics and People Analytics, particularly in forecasting, variance analysis, KPI development, and scenario modeling. 

  • Ability to work with a high degree of autonomy, prioritize effectively in alignment with stakeholders, and solve complex challenges through a data-driven and AI-enabled approach. 

  • Strong expertise with analytics and reporting tools (e.g., Excel, BI tools, or spreadsheet solutions), along with a passion for continuously improving processes, models, and analyses through automation, standardization, and AI. 

  • Ability to translate complex data into clear insights, impactful visualizations, and actionable recommendations for a variety of stakeholders across Finance, People & Culture, and Management. 

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills and a genuine interest in shaping and improving processes, tools, and strategies at a departmental level. 

  • High level of initiative, ownership, and a proactive, solution-oriented mindset. 

  • Fluency in English is required; German language skills are a strong advantage. 


What's next?

Does it sound exciting? -  Apply with your CV in English or German. Please don’t shy away if you don’t meet all the requirements! We’re looking forward to meeting you.  

We will get back to you within 14 days of receiving your application.   

The interview process includes: a 30min intro call with a TA Partner, a 60min conversation with two stakeholders and an approx. 45min Team interview. Please note the process might alter depending on our team’s availability.

WHAT WE OFFER 

More than a workplace. A place to grow. 🌍 

At Unzer, colleagues from 50+ nationalities across four countries work together to create better outcomes for our merchants. We take ownership, move with pace and keep raising the bar—as one team. 

We set high expectations and give you the flexibility, learning opportunities and practical support to do your best work, grow your impact, and build a sustainable career. 

🏡 Flexibility that works 
Combine focused time at home with connection and collaboration in the office. Our hybrid setup includes two office days per week. 

🚲 Your commute, your choice 
Choose the mobility benefit that works for you: bike leasing or a Deutschlandticket.  

🏖️ Work from anywhere in the EU 
Change your perspective and work from another EU country for up to 15 days per year. 

📗 Keep raising the bar 
Use an annual learning budget of €1,000 for courses, conferences, certifications and other development opportunities that help you grow and increase your impact.  

🫴 Support when you need it 
Access confidential counselling whenever you need support with personal or professional matters. 

💰 Build your future 
Look ahead with our company pension scheme and take care of your long-term financial wellbeing. 

 

Benefits may vary by location and employment setup. Your recruiter will share the details relevant to your role.

Please refrain from including your picture and age with the application.
