description:
This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.

About the Venture

AI models have moved faster than most companies’ ability to put them to work. The capabilities are there; knowing how to combine them effectively is still catching up.

Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist, even before the next generation arrives. That is the opportunity we are building around.

We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the right combination for the task. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the result against agreed quality standards. Think ten specialists working on ten pieces, rather than one generalist carrying the whole task.

Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.

Our founder was selected for Slush 20 Under 20, awarded by Anthropic, Slush, Index Ventures and Sifted, and brings considerable drive, a hands-on approach and a strong sense of urgency to building the company. Two things define the technical challenge here. Efficiency is the product itself, so routing, fine-tuning, caching, quantization and open-weight serving sit at the heart of the roadmap. Agentic engineering is also central to how we work. You will set the standard for using individual agents and entire agent fleets effectively, building the harnesses and workflows that allow a small team to move quickly while retaining sound engineering judgement.

There is a lot to build and an ambitious timeline ahead. We work with relentless intensity, move quickly from decisions to execution and look for people who take initiative and see things through. You will have the scope to make consequential decisions early, and the responsibility to turn them into something that works.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the engineering team: guide our founding AI engineer and backend platform engineer, review their work and establish the engineering and operational standards, including on-call and incident response.

  • Represent the company technically: bring depth and clarity to customer pilots, enterprise security reviews and investor conversations.

About You

You have grown into engineering leadership without losing the instinct to build. When faced with a difficult problem, you explore what would make it possible and look for a workable path through it, weighing failure modes alongside unit economics. AI has changed how you work, and you have taken the time to understand where it helps, where it fails and how to use it well.

We are looking for depth in five areas:

  • Backend and platform engineering: you bring deep experience in distributed systems, API design, streaming, Postgres, Kubernetes, Terraform and cloud operations, with a broad understanding of what makes a platform reliable and scalable. You have taken systems into production, operated them under significant load and worked through incidents yourself.

  • Agentic engineering: you build on strong coding fundamentals, with practical experience running agent fleets and designing and benchmarking their harnesses. You can reason independently about the code they produce and take responsibility for its quality.

  • Experience with European cloud providers such as Scaleway, Hetzner or OVH.

  • Experience working in startups tackling similar technical challenges.

Why Join

With the pre-seed round closed and the first steps already taken, you will join at a point where there is momentum to build on and considerable room to shape what comes next. You will build alongside the founder, choose and grow the engineering team, and receive co-founder equity in the business you help create.

The architecture, efficiency engine, security model and engineering culture are all still yours to shape. The decisions you make now will become the foundations for everything that follows.

We are entering a market where competitors have larger teams, more funding and an earlier start. Our conviction is that technical depth, focused decisions and a small team that works well together give us a meaningful opportunity to compete. For the right person, that is an interesting challenge to take on, with substantial ownership over how we approach it.

This is a full-time commitment, based in our Berlin office five days a week, starting as soon as possible.

title: Senior Manager, Regulatory Inspections and Strategic Response
description:
Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

The Role


This is a newly created role sitting at the centre of some of Checkout.com's most sensitive and consequential regulatory moments. Reporting to the Director of External Affairs, the Senior Manager, Regulatory Inspections and Strategic Response will manage Checkout's most important regulatory situations end-to-end, whether planned or unplanned.

In practice, that means two connected mandates. The first is the planned, cyclical work of running Checkout's regulatory inspections and examinations — a methodical, deadline-driven discipline that forms the steady-state core of the role. The second is the unplanned work: leading the response to the exceptional, time-critical and commercially sensitive situations that require a calm cross-functional leader to bring them to a resolution.

You will be the person the business turns to when a regulator opens an inspection, and when a sensitive cross-functional situation needs to be stabilised quickly and handled with judgement. You will bring order and momentum to ambiguous, high-stakes matters, coordinating across Legal, Compliance, Risk, Commercial, Product, Tech and Communications, and you will own the strategy and the outcome.

This is a role with a clear mandate to build. You will establish the function, set the operating model, and over the course of 2027 hire and develop a small team of specialists to scale it.

Our Team

Our team of 100+ is based across London, Oxford, San Sebastián and Sydney, with our primary hub in Islington (London).


Functions of the Role

This senior position operates at the critical intersection of sub-Kelvin sub-system electronics and quantum processor architectures, directly addressing the interconnect bottleneck in scalable quantum computing systems. The role spans the full digital IC design cycle—including initial microarchitecture specification, RTL development, Verilog-AMS co-simulation, physical implementation (PnR/CTS), low-power synthesis, static timing analysis (STA), and full tape-out signoff. The ultimate objective is the realization of ultra-low-power, high-density cryogenic control ICs tailored for fault-tolerant quantum computing scale-out.

  • Design Scope:  Full Lifecycle (RTL Development, AMS Co-Simulation, Physical Implementation, Low-Power Synthesis, and Tape-Out Signoff)

  • Design Tools: Proven proficiency with industry-standard EDA toolchains (e.g., Cadence Virtuoso/Innovus/Xcelium, Synopsys Design Compiler) for mixed-signal simulation, synthesis, and verification.

  • Physical Layout: Demonstrated capability in transforming RTL into GDSII/OASIS physical layouts, floorplanning, power grid synthesis, clock tree synthesis (CTS), multi-corner multi-mode static timing analysis (MCMM STA), and physical signoff (DRC/LVS/ERC).

  • Communication & Logic Design: Experience architecting high-speed serial interconnect protocols (e.g., custom SPI, AXI, SerDes) and complex finite-state machine (FSM) control logic.

  • Low Power & Thermal Management: Deep expertise in low-power dissipation techniques (clock gating, power gating, dynamic voltage scaling) within stringent thermal lift budgets of cryogenic cooling systems.

Outcome – customers who trust us at every level. Every plant has a clear owner, and an escalation route that solves problems before they reach our exec team. You've built a clean handover from Sales and a voice for Deployment in which plants we take on.

Outcome – post-sales solved. With our sales leader, you've set up how we run every plant after evaluation, and it works, with clear responsibilities mapped out. We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

Wayve’s Robot Software group turns new vehicle programs into stable, reliable robot systems. The Platform Integration team works at the boundary between onboard software and vehicle hardware, bringing up new platforms while building reusable components and frameworks that make every future integration faster and more predictable.

As a Software Engineer on the Platform Integration team, you’ll combine hands-on vehicle and bench work with production software development. Your work will directly enable safe, scalable deployment across multiple vehicle programs.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Support software bring-up on benches, HiL systems, and vehicles, including work at international test locations.

  • Develop and maintain vehicle-facing software components and shared frameworks.

  • Diagnose integration issues across software and hardware boundaries and drive them through resolution.

  • Identify architectural improvements that reduce bespoke work and improve reuse.

  • Build diagnostics, tooling, and metrics for robot-software reliability and performance.

  • Produce clear documentation and runbooks for long-term supportability.

  • Collaborate with hardware, safety, controls, calibration, and reliability teams.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • New vehicle-program bring-up across embedded compute, sensors, networks, and software services.

  • Linux-based robotic and automotive systems with multi-process and distributed architectures.

  • ROS2 or similar middleware, node development, message interfaces, and system integration.

  • Sensor calibration, synchronisation, data validation, and system-level debugging.

  • Automotive-grade compute platforms such as NVIDIA DRIVE and Qualcomm Snapdragon Ride.

  • Vehicle communication systems including CAN and Automotive Ethernet.

  • Shared abstractions and frameworks that improve reliability across programs.

 

🙌 You should apply if

  • You have strong software-development experience in C++, Python, or Rust.

  • You have delivered production-quality software on Linux-based robotic, embedded, or automotive platforms.

  • You understand ROS2 or similar robotics middleware and distributed-system integration.

  • You have hands-on experience integrating software with vehicle or embedded hardware.

  • You can diagnose complex problems using logs, telemetry, on-target tests, and systematic experimentation.

  • You understand vehicle sensors, networking, and the practical realities of platform bring-up.

Experience with drive-by-wire systems, CAN tools, shared frameworks, HiL or simulation, functional safety, technical documentation, or observability would be valuable.

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalize and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial recruiter screen — 25 mins

  • Competency Interviews — Programming and technical domain (2 hours)

  • Deep-dive technical interviews — Programming and hiring-manager/team fit (2 hours)

  • Final interview — Mission and values alignment (30 mins)

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

title: Junior Market Data Analyst – Chartering
description:
At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors.

Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 700 experts from 35+ countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success.


Your future position

Join Kpler’s Chartering team as a Junior Market Data Analyst – Chartering and play a key role in ensuring the quality and accuracy of the data that powers our Chartering products.

Kpler’s Chartering products rely on accurate vessel, ownership and market data to help charterers, shipowners and brokers make informed commercial decisions. In this role, you will work hands-on with the datasets behind these products, investigating inconsistencies, validating information and helping improve data quality at scale.

Your work will span a range of chartering datasets, from vessel ownership and characteristics to fixtures, cargo orders, vessel positions and shipping zones. You will use SQL and Python to extract, transform and analyse data, build validation checks and investigate potential issues. 

This is a role for someone who enjoys getting into the detail of data, asking why something doesn't look right and finding ways to identify and solve problems systematically. You will work closely with Product, Data, Research, Engineering and AI/ML teams, turning individual data issues into broader improvements across Kpler's datasets and products.


Your mission is to:
  • Monitor, validate and improve the quality of key datasets supporting Kpler's Chartering products.
  • Investigate data gaps, inconsistencies and customer-reported issues, using data analysis to understand their root causes and drive them through to resolution.
  • Curate and validate vessel ownership, commercial management, operator information and relevant vessel characteristics.
  • Review and benchmark AI-parsed fixtures, identifying recurring extraction errors and building validation approaches to measure and improve parsing quality.
  • Use SQL to query large datasets, including cargo and AIS data, to investigate potential issues and identify incorrect or inconsistent information at scale.
  • Use Python notebooks to extract, transform and analyse data and develop validation scripts and repeatable quality checks.
  • Maintain and improve Kpler's chartering-specific shipping zones and geographical mappings, using tools such as QGIS.
  • Work with Product, Data, Research, Engineering and AI/ML teams to provide structured feedback and help improve the quality of underlying datasets and extraction processes.
  • Translate individual data-quality issues into systematic improvements where appropriate, identifying patterns rather than only correcting individual records.
  • Contribute to the development of new analytical views and algorithms as the Chartering product evolves, including areas such as CPP/DPP and projected vessels.
  • Help establish and track data-quality metrics, benchmarks and processes as Chartering datasets expand.

    • Experience & Background:
  • 1–3 years of experience in data analysis, market research, maritime/shipping, commodities or a related analytical role.
  • Proven hands-on experience with SQL and confidence writing queries to analyse and investigate large datasets.
  • Proven hands-on experience with Python, including working in notebooks and using Python for data analysis, transformation or validation.
  • Strong Excel / Google Sheets skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with excellent attention to detail and an ability to identify patterns and inconsistencies in data.
  • Comfortable working with large datasets and extracting and transforming data to investigate specific questions
    • Desirable:
  • Understanding of shipping, chartering or commodity markets.
  • Familiarity with tanker and/or dry-bulk vessel segments.
  • Understanding of concepts such as fixtures, vessel positions, cargo orders, vessel ownership and shipping geography.
  • Experience working with AI/LLM-extracted or other machine-generated datasets.
  • Experience with maritime data providers, brokers, shipowners, charterers or commodity trading companies.

Because CarbonX materials physically behave differently from standard graphite during dispersion and calendering, you will play a crucial role in diagnosing processability, optimising slurry formulations, and ensuring defect-free electrode production.

• Operational Troubleshooting & QC: Enforce strict quality control standards. Identify root causes of material or coating deviations and execute real-time operational problem-solving.

• Lab Equipment Ownership: Manage, calibrate, and maintain key equipment (different types of mixers, coating/calendering lines, diagnostic tools), manage routine calibration and preventative maintenance, and draft practical SOPs.

• EHS Rigor: Maintain a clean, organised, and safe laboratory environment, strictly following chemical handling and safety protocols.

• Educational Background: Bachelor's (BSc), HBO, or MBO in Materials Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related practical scientific discipline.

Ready to take proven deep-tech to industrial scale?

The technology is no longer just an idea—it has been produced at scale, integrated into commercial processes, tested in cells, and validated by major customers. Ready to stop working on theoretical projects and help build something that’s actually shipping?

Every day, patients, physicians, and pharma companies navigate a fragmented, slow, and complex healthcare ecosystem to find pre-approval treatments. As our Chief Financial Officer (CFO), based at our Amsterdam headquarters, you will be a central member of the Leadership Team and a close strategic partner to the CEO. You will not simply run a finance function. You will build the financial infrastructure, governance, and discipline that this next chapter of growth demands, across a business spanning technology, regulated healthcare services, and multiple jurisdictions.

The Challenges

As CFO, you will step into the trenches to tackle four defining challenges:

  • Leading buy-side M&A execution: You will be the primary financial architect behind our inorganic growth. As myTomorrows evaluates acquisitions and strategic partnerships to complement organic growth, you will lead deal structuring, due diligence, valuation, and integration from a buyer's seat, bringing real process discipline to a company entering its first phase of consolidation.

  • Architecting for multi-jurisdiction complexity: You will own the financial structure connecting our operations across the Netherlands, the US, and India. This means building robust transfer pricing policies, intercompany arrangements, and multi-party revenue recognition frameworks that hold up to investor and regulatory scrutiny as the business scales across borders.

  • Being a credible investor partner: You will serve as the finance function's primary interface to our Supervisory Board. You will bring investor-grade reporting rhythms, board governance discipline, and the judgment to translate operational reality into the language our sponsor and Board expect.

  • Preparing for future fundraising and exit: You will help set the company up for its next capital event, whether that is a follow-on raise, a strategic sale, or another form of exit. This means building the financial track record, audit readiness, and data room discipline that institutional buyers and investors expect, well ahead of any process actually starting.

What You Bring to the Table

Experience & Technical Depth

  • Proven CFO or strong CFO-1 experience in a high-growth, investor-backed business, ideally in healthtech, healthcare services, life sciences, or another complex international platform environment.

  • Buy-side M&A execution is a firm requirement. You have led acquisitions from the buyer's side, not only sell-side or advisory M&A, and can speak credibly to deal structuring, diligence, and post-deal integration.

  • Multi-jurisdiction financial complexity: hands-on experience with transfer pricing, intercompany structures, and multi-party revenue recognition across at least two of the following: Europe, the US, and Asia.

  • Institutional governance familiarity: direct experience with board reporting rhythms, supervisory board obligations, and the accountability that comes with a private equity or growth equity sponsor.

  • Regulated sector navigation: exposure to compliance-intensive environments, ideally in healthcare, life sciences, or another highly regulated domain.

  • Leading a lean senior team: you have led finance at this scale and know how to raise the ceiling of a small team rather than solving it with headcount.

  • Fundraising and exit experience: you have run or closely supported a capital raise, whether equity, debt, or both, and ideally have direct exposure to a sale process, IPO, or other exit event. You know what "diligence-ready" actually means in practice.

  • A Strategic Connector: You translate financial complexity into a clear narrative for the CEO, Supervisory Board, and cross-functional leaders, building alignment and confidence in the numbers.

The Financial Foundation Today

You will inherit a finance function with a solid FP&A core and real scope to build:

  • Structure: A multi-entity organization spanning the Netherlands, the US, and an operational hub in India, with growing cross-border complexity.

  • Team: A lean, capable team of five. A finance lead as your direct report with three people behind her, plus Revenue Operations, giving you direct influence over pipeline, forecasting, and pricing rather than a view from the sidelines.

  • Reporting: FP&A and performance reporting capability already in place; the priority now is professionalizing controls, governance, and investor-grade reporting infrastructure around it.

  • Ownership: A Supervisory Board and a committed institutional sponsor, Avego Healthcare Capital, with clear expectations on growth economics, capital allocation, and value creation.

  • Growth model: Organic growth complemented by inorganic opportunities, with M&A and strategic partnerships expected to play an increasing role in the company's next phase.

  • When you look back at your first year and a half, you will have successfully:

  • Led or materially advanced one or more buy-side M&A processes, demonstrating deal discipline from sourcing through integration.

  • Established a robust multi-jurisdiction financial architecture, including transfer pricing policy and intercompany structures that hold up under scrutiny.

  • Built investor-grade financial governance and greater confidence in data quality across the business.

  • Strengthened the finance team and its standing with business leaders, while building on the FP&A foundation already in place.

  • Become a trusted partner to the CEO and Supervisory Board, with a reporting rhythm that meets institutional ownership expectations.

  • Helped shape a clear financial roadmap for international scale and long-term value creation.

What we Offer

  • A Seat at the Table: Autonomy to shape the financial architecture of a category-defining company with deep strategic relevance.

  • Stability + Speed: The financial backing of a leading healthcare investment fund, paired with the agility and creativity of a global scale-up.

  • Comprehensive Executive Benefits: Competitive base salary, performance-driven annual bonus, and a substantial Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP).

    You'll build documentation, enablement programmes, design resources and governance models that help global and regional teams confidently apply OLX Group's brand standards.

    You'll influence senior stakeholders across Product, Marketing and Executive Leadership, aligning teams around a shared creative vision and ensuring design has a meaningful voice in strategic decision-making.

  • Expertise in Figma and/or Adobe Creative Suite

title: Power Markets Analyst (f/m/d)
description:
About Nexun

Backed by Marguerite, a leading pan-European infrastructure fund, Nexun is a fast-growing renewable project development platform active in Spain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and Austria. At Nexun, we are passionate advocates for renewable energy as well as grid infrastructure and are committed to accelerating the transition to a low-carbon economy. Join our diverse team to contribute to projects that positively impact communities across Europe.

The Power/Flexibility Markets Analyst leads the commercial development, negotiation, and optimization of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects, including both standalone storage assets and co-located solar-plus-storage projects. The role focuses on identifying best value and route-to-market for our projects, forecasting revenue schemes and offtake contracts possibilities (Tolling Agreements, PPAs), optimizing the commercial design of our plants to derisk projects and maximize their value at the point of sale (RTB) based on a solid market and technical understanding of electricity markets and asset configurations, negotiating PPAs and Tolling agreements.

Target countries: Italy, Poland, France as priority and Spain, Austria and Germany as secondary markets

Tasks

  • Develop and maintain in-depth knowledge of the electricity markets in at least one of the target countries, including Day-Ahead, Intraday, Ancillary Services, Balancing Markets, Capacity Markets.
  • Monitor regulatory and market developments and evaluate their impact on the revenues and commercial viability of BESS and solar projects.
  • Collect, analyze, and develop electricity price forecasts and revenue projections for standalone BESS and hybrid solar-plus-storage projects.
  • Analyze and compare current route-to-market and optimization models and select and negotiate the optimal role (merchant, tolling, PPA, floor/hybrid structures) for standalone BESS, co-located BESS with photovoltaic (PV) plants, and hybrid renewable energy projects to maximize the RTB value and derisk the projects.
  • Originate, negotiate, and close Tolling Agreements and Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with offtakers, utilities, traders, on all type of assets (BESS; collocated etc.)
  • Support the preparation of business cases, investment decisions, financial models, and technical/commercial due diligence processes.
  • Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders across the BESS ecosystem and the different target countries, including utilities, energy traders, optimizers, aggregators, transmission and distribution system operators, regulatory authorities, investors, and asset operators.
  • Evaluate and optimize different technical system configurations from both a commercial and market perspective to maximize the RTB value (duration, sizing, PV/BESS ratio etc.)
  • Collaborate closely with Development, Engineering, Finance, and external partners throughout the project lifecycle.

Requirements

Technical Qualifications

  • Good understanding of electricity markets in at least one European target market.
  • Familiarity with Day-Ahead, Intraday, Balancing, Ancillary Services, Capacity Markets, and other flexibility markets.
  • Understanding of current revenue optimization and commercialization models for standalone BESS and co-located renewable energy projects.
  • Ability to interpret and use market models, revenue forecasts, and financial models.
  • Strong Excel skills and financial modeling capabilities
  • Familiarity with Python, Power BI, or similar tools is a plus.
  • Exposure to commercial negotiations, tolling agreements, PPAs, or energy trading is beneficial but not mandatory.

Analytical Capabilities

The successful candidate should be able to quantitatively assess how different technical configurations impact project economics. Typical analyses include:

  • Comparing 2-hour and 4-hour battery storage systems with respect to CAPEX, OPEX, revenue potential, and Internal Rate of Return (IRR).
  • Determining the optimal battery size for co-located solar PV projects.
  • Evaluating revenue allocation across energy arbitrage, balancing services, ancillary services, and other flexibility products.
  • Performing scenario and sensitivity analyses covering electricity price forecasts, technology cost reductions, grid connection costs, financing assumptions, and regulatory changes.

Personal Competencies

  • Strong commercial and negotiation skills; proven ability to lead and close deals
  • Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills.
  • Self-driven, proactive, and entrepreneurial mindset.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Fluent English (written and spoken); additional European languages are considered an advantage.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Energy Economics, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Finance, or related discipline.

5-8 years of experience in commercial or offtake origination, PPA/tolling negotiation, route-to-market, or energy trading, combined with a solid understanding of electricity markets and BESS & all renewable assets. A demonstrable deal track record is highly desirable

At Nexun, you’ll be part of a mission-driven, international organization shaping the future of renewable energy across Europe. Depending on the country you work in, you benefit from market-leading compensation and locally relevant benefits. We provide:

About WeTravel

Travel gives people new experiences and brings them together, sometimes in life-changing ways. That's especially the case for group travel and multi-day travel (think of a 7-day safari in the Serengeti, a 5-day scuba diving trip in the Galápagos, or a multi-week pilgrimage) where travelers get to really immerse themselves. Passionate travel organizers make this magic happen, and WeTravel is here to support them.

Multi-day travel businesses use WeTravel as their end-to-end operating system: publishing trip offerings, generating and converting leads, processing payments around the world, paying suppliers and vendors. WeTravel helps them grow sales, save time, and save money, so they can focus on delivering incredible bucket-list experiences.

WeTravel is a 400+ person company representing more than 50 countries. We combine global diversity with the agility and closeness of a much smaller team. More than 90 colleagues are based in our Amsterdam office in Rokin, including the entire Product Org and most of our Engineering team.

You will have fun innovating fast with brilliant, low-ego colleagues. Our clients are also easy to reach, which helps us stay close to their needs and build with them.

Financially, WeTravel is highly secure and growing fast, with 50 to 100 percent year-over-year growth depending on the metric. This gives us a strong foundation to build from.

About the Role

This is the domain where our biggest bet is playing out. Building and selling a great multi-day trip is a lot of work: crafting a story worth booking, assembling the content that tells it, and presenting it all in a page a traveler trusts. Our goal is to cut that turnaround down so organizers get back to their client faster, convert more of them, and sell more trips. It also has to hold up as they grow, because a boutique agency selling bespoke trips and a student travel operator running hundreds of departures are building on the same tools. The way we get there is great technology in the hands of organizers and their teams. You will own that end to end, the experience and the engine behind it.

What you'll work on

WeTravel Trips give organizers the tools to create proposals, detailed itineraries and a high-conversion booking experience, while giving them time back to grow and operate their business.

We're now looking for a Staff PM to take this domain through its next phase of growth, and make WeTravel the best software for travel businesses to build, present and sell their trips.

Our success in this domain will drive the growth of our organizers by expanding in several areas:

  • An integrated building experience that helps organizers find the right content and craft the right trip for the right travelers.

  • Shared libraries that pay off most when a team works from them, so every proposal that leaves the company is consistent, beautiful, and unmistakably theirs, whoever wrote it.

  • AI-enabled tools to imagine and create new trips, produce world class content, and optimize their sales funnel.

  • Trip pages organizers can publish and promote wherever their travelers are.

1/ Designing the trip page and selling the trip

Think of the trip page as the product detail page of the travel industry. It is where an organizer's work becomes something a traveler wants, understands, and buys.

  • Dynamic Trip Builder: Intuitive tools for organizers to create their trip offerings, in the languages their travelers read, on WeTravel and beyond it.

  • Day by day itineraries: the plan that makes a trip feel real before anyone has booked it, built fast and kept accurate as the trip changes.

  • High converting pages and proposals: whether an organizer publishes a trip for the world or sends a tailored proposal to one client, the result has to look professional, capture travelers' imaginations, and turn interest into a booking.

  • Mobile app for travelers: once they have booked, travelers carry the trip page in their pocket, with everything they need before and during it.

2/ The content and AI engine that turns hours of work into minutes

  • WeTravel Library: a curated library of properties, activities, and reusable content on its way to 20,000 properties, so organizers build with high quality content.

  • The organizer's own library: their photos, their descriptions, their reusable blocks, so a growing team sells in one voice instead of rewriting content from scratch.

  • AI-assisted building: Copilot that drafts and improves trips inside the builder, so organizers start from a strong draft rather than an empty page.

And the team behind it. Our content specialists will report to you, and you will own the content strategy, the regional prioritization, and the pipeline that keeps the library growing.

I'm looking for an experienced, generalist product manager to lead this domain end-to-end. You will deeply study travel organizers' needs, prioritize them, come up with solutions (or hypotheses to test), drive all necessary functions to build and launch the solutions, drive adoption, and ultimately grow our revenue and profit. You will also manage our content team, and you will have direct and continuous access to C-level executives to ideate and create products.

If you've ever wanted to empower businesses with innovative tech and have fun in a well-funded rocketship in the heart of Amsterdam, this is it.

An Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate would bring a track record of exceptional results and a well-rounded product management skill set, especially the ability to break down any problem and drive high-velocity execution.

Must-haves:

  • Deep product management experience owning real outcomes, not just execution.

    • 10+ years in product management is ideal (for staff level)

    • 7+ years is minimum (for senior level)

  • Travel industry knowledge.

  • Comfortable being accountable for product-led commercial outcomes, not just features shipped.

  • Strong cross-functional stakeholder leadership across sales / account management, engineering, design.

  • Growth and experimentation mindset, with the judgment to decide without perfect data. Willing to ship, learn, and iterate.

  • Data self-sufficient. You can pull your own numbers, find where a funnel leaks, and size the opportunity before asking for engineering time.

Things that will likely help you in this particular role:

  • You have owned a builder, editor or CMS-like product where the artifact your users create is what earns them money.

  • You have shipped AI features that people kept using, and you can tell the difference between a good demo and real adoption.

  • You have treated content as product, not as someone else's job, and have worked with or led a content operation.

  • Experience with public APIs, webhooks, or platform work.

  • Experience managing people, even a small team or a dotted line.

Interview process

Our process aims to be high-signal and help you learn about WeTravel and our people. Two interviews will be realistic working sessions. No take-home assignments. The whole process will take only a few weeks.

Screen

  • Recruiter screen (30 min): introduction, background, motivation.

1st round

  • Hiring manager interview (60 min): your background in depth, the role, your questions.

2nd round

  • Live whiteboard session (60 min, onsite): a real Trips decision worked through together, for example Trip page redesign, Copilot scope, or Library content prioritization. Assesses structured thinking, clear reasoning out loud, and product judgment under incomplete information.

  • Team working session (45 min): with a Product Manager, an Engineering Manager, and a Designer: Working through your product management experience, plus a UX collaboration exercise.

3rd round

  • CEO conversation (30 min): A two-way discussion about mission, ambition, and culture.


A Final Note

Our clients are entrepreneurs and artisans who pour their passion into creating bucket-list experiences. Helping them grow their businesses is what motivates us, and what would motivate the right PM for the Trips domain. If that resonates, I'd love to meet you.

Steven

title: Account Executive (m/f/d)
description:
Standort: München
Art: Vollzeit

Sales an Vertriebsteams in Enterprises ist die Champions League - und Bliro ist dein Ticket rein. Du verkaufst an Enterprise-Unternehmen, lernst von einem Team, das genau das schon macht, und wirst Teil einer Growth-Story.

About Bliro

Bei Bliro revolutionieren wir den Arbeitsalltag von Außendienstteams mithilfe von KI. 2.5 Millionen Außendienstler allein in Deutschland verlieren täglich Stunden an manuelle Nachbereitung. Bliro löst genau das - mit Transkription und den KI-Voice-Agents Vicky und Tim, die Kundengespräche vor-und nachbereiten, Besuchsberichte dokumentieren und das CRM in Echtzeit aktualisieren. Per Sprache wird so die gesamte Schreibtischarbeit automatisiert und der Außendienst gesteuert.

Schon heute vertrauen über 2.000 Unternehmen auf Bliro - darunter schnell wachsende Start-ups, etablierte Corporates und mittelständische Unternehmen (z.B. igus, Lanxess und Telefonica Deutschland). Unterstützt von Top-Investoren, suchen wir nun dich als Vollzeitmitglied im Bereich Account Executive (AE), um unser Wachstum weiter voranzutreiben.

Unser Sales Team bringt Erfahrung aus den schnellstwachsenden Software Unternehmen der Welt (Ex-Deel, Ex-Autodesk, Ex-Celonis) und eigenen Unternehmensgründungen mit!

👇 Sieh selbst, was du an Vertriebsteams verkaufen wirst:

🎯 Deine Aufgaben

Als Account Executive bei Bliro verantwortest du den gesamten Sales-Cycle - von der Demo bis zum Abschluss. Du arbeitest Hand in Hand mit unserem SDR-Team, das deinen Kalender mit qualifizierten Demos füllt, damit du dich auf das konzentrieren kannst, was du am besten kannst: Deals zu closen.

  1. Sales-Prozess führen und gewinnen

  • Du leitest Discovery Calls und maßgeschneiderte Produkt-Demos mit Mid-Market- und Enterprise-Prospects.

  • Du baust starke Beziehungen zu Key Stakeholdern und Entscheider:innen auf.

  • Du steuerst komplexe Sales-Cycles und verhandelst Verträge mit ACVs von 50k€+.

  1. Mit dem gesamten Go-to-Market-Team zusammenarbeiten

  • Du arbeitest eng mit den SDRs zusammen, die deine Termine buchen - für einen reibungslosen Handoff und enge Zusammenarbeit.

  • Arbeite eng mit dem Customer Success Team für reibungslose Handoffs sowie mit Growth zur Schärfung unserer GTM-Strategie.

  • Du teilst Feedback aus dem Feld, um unsere Roadmap mitzugestalten.

  1. Quota übertreffen und Wachstum vorantreiben

  • Du clost konsequent neues Business, um die ambitionierten Ziele zu erreichen - und zu übertreffen.

  • Du baust deine Pipeline in Schlüsselbranchen und -regionen aus.

  • Du positionierst Bliro als vertrauenswürdigen Partner für Kunden, die ihre Vertriebsprozesse mit KI transformieren wollen.

🧠 Dein Profil

Wir suchen motivierte AEs, die für High-Touch-B2B-SaaS-Sales brennen und mit einem kategoriedefinierenden AI-Startup wachsen wollen.

Das solltest du mitbringen:

  • Nachweisliche Erfolge im Abschluss von Mid-Market- und Enterprise-SaaS-Deals (ACVs von 50k€ und mehr).

  • Erfahrung in der Verantwortung des gesamten Sales-Cycles - vom Erstgespräch bis zum unterschriebenen Vertrag.

  • Exzellente Kommunikations- und Beziehungsfähigkeiten im Umgang mit verschiedenen Stakeholdern.

  • Hohe Eigenmotivation, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und Team-first-Mentalität.

  • Fließende Deutsch- (C2) und Englischkenntnisse (C1+).

Nice to have:

  • Erfahrung mit direkter Exposure zu C-Level, Sales Leadern und IT - nicht nur komplexen Stakeholder-Settings im Allgemeinen.

  • Erfahrung im Verkauf an den industriellen Mittelstand in DACH.

💡 Warum Bliro

🚀 Klarer Karrierepfad - kein Blindflug
Bei uns weißt du von Tag 1, wohin die Reise geht. Als AE übernimmst du von Anfang an echte Deals, echte Kunden und echte Verantwortung. Wer kontinuierlich seine Targets hitted, kann sich bei uns in Richtung Senior AE oder Sales Lead weiterentwickeln. Kein Versprechen ins Blaue, sondern ein klarer Plan.

💸 Vergütung + Extras, die sich sehen lassen können
Bei uns bekommst du ein wettbewerbsfähiges Fixgehalt, einen variablen Bonus ohne Deckel, VSOPs, Deutschlandticket, Wellpass sowie Essen und Trinken im Office. Dein Einsatz wird direkt belohnt. Learning Budget? Haben wir. Sales-Library? Klar. Persönliches Coaching, das dich aufs nächste Level bringt? Auch dabei.

🌍 30+ Köpfe, 10+ Länder, ein Netzwerk
Bei uns triffst du auf Kreativität und Internationalität. Du arbeitest mit Menschen, die mitdenken, mitlachen und mit dir wachsen wollen. Außerdem bringt unser Team bringt Erfahrung aus den schnellstwachsenden Software-Unternehmen der Welt mit. Dazu profitierst du von unserem starken Netzwerk im Münchner Startup-Ecosystem - mit Verbindungen zu VCs und Gründern.

📍 Office-Lage, die kaum zu toppen ist

Unser Büro sitzt direkt über dem Augustiner Stammhaus - mitten in München. Ob Mittagspause mit Blick auf die Stadt oder schnelles Feierabendbier um die Ecke: bessere Nachbarschaft gibt's kaum.

🥳 Echter Teamspirit, jeden Monat

Wir warten nicht auf den Jahres-Offsite. Bei Bliro gibt's monatliche Team-Events - von Minigolf und Bowling über Burrito Nights bis Pickleball. Spontane Lunches und Coffee Breaks inklusive.

🧑‍💻 Flexibel
9 to 5 ist nicht dein Ding? Kein Problem. Ob vom Küchentisch oder aus dem Office - bei uns zählt das Ergebnis, nicht der Aufenthaltsort. Und ja, auch Pyjamahosen sind im Homeoffice offiziell erlaubt.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑 You'll never close alone

Dein Start bei Bliro wird begleitet von einem Buddy, der dich einführt, auffängt und mit Memes versorgt. Wir sind Teamplayer - von Tag eins bis zu deinem ersten erfolgreichen Closing (und darüber hinaus).

Du hast Lust, den Vertrieb eines KI-Startups von Grund auf mitzuerleben und mitzugestalten? Dann bewirb dich jetzt!

description:

  • Background: Idealerweise hast du erste praktische Erfahrung im Online-Marketing, einer (Media-)Agentur, im HR-Marketing/Employer Branding oder einem vergleichbaren Umfeld – auch motivierte Quereinsteiger*innen sind bei uns herzlich willkommen!

Wir sind längst mehr als eine Lern-App - StudySmarter begleitet Millionen Menschen von der Schule über das Studium bis in den Berufseinstieg. Dabei bewegen wir uns an der Schnittstelle aus Tech, Social Impact und internationalem Wachstum: Wir setzen früh auf neue Technologien, insbesondere KI, und entwickeln Produkt und Prozesse kontinuierlich weiter. Our mission is ambitious and we can’t do it alone - join Abacum as we build the future of Business Planning!

We are looking for...

An enterprise seller who already knows the Office of the CFO. You've carried a number selling planning, EPM, FP&A or finance software. You know how a CFO buys, how a steering committee stalls, and how to get a multi-stakeholder deal signed.

At Abacum you'll own a named territory of enterprise and upper mid-market accounts across EMEA. Many of them run legacy planning tools or spreadsheets that can't keep up with the business. Your job is to show them a better foundation, and win.

- Forecast with discipline and keep a clean pipeline in CRM

- Work with Solutions Engineering, Product and Leadership to shape deals, and feed what you hear in the market back into the roadmap

What we need...

title: Senior Backend Developer (Python, Java)
description:
Legal AI is only as good as the knowledge behind it. At Lefebvre Sdu, we've been building that knowledge for over 200 years. Day in, day out. Law by law. Word by word. As the Dutch heart of Lefebvre Group, the European leader in legal and tax knowledge, we're also developing our own platform: GenIA-L, where lawyers and tax advisors don't just get an answer, but an answer they're willing to attach their name to. More than 75,000 professionals use it daily, generating over 100 million euros in ARR across Europe. We're looking for a Senior Backend Developer to help build that.

HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD

Our Knowledge Team is the layer between the content and the AI. We pull in millions of documents from internal databases, public sources, and the web, standardize them, and make them usable for the AI agents that distill answers from them. The real challenge isn't storage but selection. Out of those millions of documents, exactly one paragraph needs to surface the moment a lawyer asks a question. Surface the wrong one, and the agent gives an answer that sounds plausible but is wrong. In our field, that's not a bug: it's a liability issue. What you build determines whether the answer holds up.

There's work to be done, and it's the kind of work you could talk about for a whole evening. The pipeline has been running for six years, built in Scala and Java, and parts of it deserve a new foundation. Reranking is the biggest need: determining which passage, out of a mountain of legal documents, actually answers the question being asked. Not just which one contains the matching words. That's the problem we’re solving. The team is strong on the scientific side, in retrieval, and in understanding what a model can and can't handle. What we're looking to add is engineering firepower: someone who can turn ideas into systems that deliver. Not to rebuild everything over six months just because it was once set up differently, but to see where the real gains are and start there.

  • You build and improve the pipeline that turns content into knowledge our AI agents can use.

  • You work on reranking quality, so the agent gets the right information, not just the most information.

  • You help shape the approach to retrieval and knowledge extraction, bringing in what you've seen work elsewhere.

  • You work in Python for everything new, and in Java where the existing codebase calls for it.

  • You make technical decisions, even when no one is looking over your shoulder.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You're an engineer who looks beyond the ticket. You want to understand why something is being built and what it delivers for the customer, and you're not afraid to have an opinion about it. You don't need a manager to make a technical call, and you speak up when you think something should be done differently.

  • Experience with Python and Java. Everything newly built is developed in Python, closely aligned with the AI teams who also work in it. But a large part of our current codebase runs on Java, so you need to be comfortable working with that too.

  • Experience with Elasticsearch. That's where it's determined which information the agent gets to see.

title: Computer Vision & AI Engineer - Interceptor C‑UAS (m/f/d)
description:
About the role:

At Quantum Systems, we are building highly autonomous interceptor systems that must perceive, decide, and act under extreme latency, motion, and environmental constraints.

We are looking for a Computer Vision & AI Engineer to drive the perception stack of our Counter-UAS interceptor platform. You will work on low-latency camera pipelines, small-object detection, object tracking, sensor fusion, visual odometry, precision landing, camera calibration, embedded inference, and data pipelines for training and validation.

This role is suited for someone with a strong academic or practical background in computer vision, AI, robotics, or perception systems. A Master’s degree is expected; a PhD is a strong plus. We are open to ambitious early-career candidates if they bring strong technical depth, practical implementation skills, and the ability to own complex perception problems.

Your Mission

You will develop the vision and AI pipeline that turns raw camera data into actionable perception outputs for autonomous flight. This includes low-latency detection and tracking, motion-aware vision, sensor fusion with inertial data, 3D direction-vector estimation, GPS-denied navigation, and precision landing support.


What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Bring up, optimize, and maintain high-performance camera pipelines, including CSI camera interfaces, raw image access, buffering, synchronization, and latency reduction.

  • Develop detection algorithms for small and difficult-to-see objects in moving and rotating camera images.

  • Combine machine learning and classical computer vision approaches where appropriate.

  • Fuse inertial data, motion information, and visual data to improve detection and tracking in moving image sequences.

  • Build object tracking pipelines that can switch from initial detection to low-latency tracking once a target has been acquired.

  • Optimize perception pipelines for embedded execution on NVIDIA Jetson platforms.

  • Work toward high frame-rate processing targets in the range of 100–300 FPS, where technically feasible.

  • Use camera intrinsics and extrinsics to transform image-space detections into 3D direction vectors or other navigation-relevant outputs.

  • Work on GPS-denied navigation concepts using visual odometry, including approaches with forward-facing camera views rather than only downward-looking cameras.

  • Develop visual support for precision landing, including height estimation, velocity estimation, and motion-state estimation from limited camera perspectives.

  • Build and maintain the data pipeline from onboard recordings to cloud storage, preprocessing, annotation, dataset generation, training, validation, and benchmarking.

  • Work with annotation tools such as SuperAnnotate, CVAT, Label Studio, or comparable systems.

  • Benchmark and evaluate different model and algorithm families, including approaches such as CenterNet, SuperPoint, SuperGlue, optical flow, feature tracking, object detection, and lightweight embedded models.

  • Build deployment pipelines using ONNX, TensorRT, custom inference runners, or comparable embedded inference tooling.

  • Collaborate closely with autonomy, flight control, embedded software, test, and systems engineering teams.




What you bring to the team:

  • Master’s degree or PhD in computer vision, AI, robotics, machine learning, electrical engineering, computer science, aerospace engineering, or a comparable technical field.

  • Strong understanding of computer vision fundamentals, camera geometry, feature detection, object detection, tracking, calibration, and image-space to 3D transformations.

  • Practical experience implementing computer vision or machine learning pipelines in Python and C++.

  • Experience with embedded inference, ideally on NVIDIA Jetson, CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX, GStreamer, V4L2, or similar technologies.

  • Ability to read, understand, and implement ideas from current research papers.

  • Understanding of latency, throughput, profiling, memory movement, and real-time constraints.

  • Experience with dataset creation, annotation workflows, training/validation splits, metrics, and benchmarking.

  • Strong mathematical intuition and willingness to debug both algorithms and real-world sensor data.

  • Ability to take ownership of a technical area and drive it from research prototype to flight-test-ready software.

    • Experience with UAV perception, robotics perception, visual odometry, SLAM, sensor fusion, or tracking systems.

    • Experience with IMU-camera fusion, ego-motion compensation, rolling-shutter effects, or high-frame-rate cameras.

    • Experience with precision landing, visual navigation, or GPS-denied navigation.

    • Experience building cloud-based ML training and validation pipelines.

    • Publications, thesis work, GitHub projects, demos, or competition results in computer vision, robotics, AI, or autonomous systems.

Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you dont meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.

Why Quantum-Systems:

  • Be at the forefront of next-generation Defence innovation.

  • Work in a fast-paced, agile environment where your ideas make an impact.

  • Collaborate with a team of industry pioneers who are ambitious, bold, and visionary.

  • Opportunities for individual and professional growth in a globally recognized organization.


Our benefits:

  • Flexible working hours: With trust-based working hours, you are not only responsible for your working hours, but also for your work-life balance.

  • Mobile Work: If things get a little busy in the office, you have the option to work remotely one flexible day per week to create the right balance.

About us:

Quantum Systems is a leading European deep-tech company for unmanned systems across air, land and maritime domains. We develop and scale integrated hardware, software and AI-powered solutions for mission-critical operations. By combining autonomous platforms with intelligent software and AI, Quantum Systems enables customers to operate, understand and act across domains.

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

The team works closely with the Operations, Operations Strategy and Analytics teams to deliver impactful changes across the wider Operations function. The team builds and maintains the internal systems – including tools for underwriting, notifications, and account management – that power iwoca’s German market. They support more than 70 colleagues across sales, credit, and collections who rely on these tools every day.

As the German business grows, the Operations Engineering team is moving beyond small improvements and into reworking how work is done. By reducing manual steps and improving how information flows through the company, the team directly influences how quickly other teams can act, how reliably iwoca can support its customers, and where we can most effectively spend human effort.

You’ll work on the systems that internal teams rely on to serve customers.   • Expand your scope: You’ll join a growing team that supports individual ownership, offering you opportunities to lead projects end-to-end, developing your commercial judgement.

  • Able to use lateral thinking to anticipate technical challenges and to improve existing systems that support complex workflows.

  • A data-driven mindset: Using data or metrics to assess whether changes have had the intended effect.

We expect to pay from £75,000–£90,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

title: Treasury Manager (ALM)
description:
Build with us

Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow, with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.

With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.

We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.

Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.

Your impact

Treasury is where Mollie's balance sheet takes shape, this team makes sure that our balance sheet is safe, well-funded and resilient. You, as Treasury Manager, will be one of the first people building the Asset & Liability Management (ALM) function for Mollie.

This is a genuine 0-to-1 role. There is no legacy ALM framework to maintain, no existing ILAAP to update, no established models to inherit. You'll help design and build the liquidity risk framework, the interest rate and credit spread risk approach, and the funding and balance sheet strategy. Your work will feed directly into Mollie’s licence application and, once authorised, into how Mollie actually manages its liquidity and funding risks.

You'll work closely with our product teams, Finance, and Risk Domains and your analysis will be seen by senior leadership and, eventually, by our regulator. As Mollie moves from application to operation, your scope will grow from building the framework to running it.

What you'll ship

  • Build and own the core building blocks of Mollie liquidity risk framework, including the ILAAP, LCR/NSFR monitoring, and liquidity stress testing.

  • Develop Mollie’s approach to interest rate risk and credit spread risk in the banking book (IRRBB/CSRBB), from risk identification through to models, limits and hedging strategy.

  • Contribute to the design of Mollie’s funding and balance sheet strategy, including deposit mix, funding diversification and balance sheet construction.

  • Build the Contingency Funding Plan and related early-warning indicators, so Mollie knows exactly what to do under stress before it needs to.

  • Produce clear, well-documented policies, methodologies and models that will stand up to scrutiny from DNB/ECB, external auditors, and Mollie's own second and third lines of defense.

  • Support senior leadership (ALCO or its future equivalent) with the analysis, reporting and recommendations it needs to make sound balance sheet decisions.

  • Partner with Risk, Finance and our external advisors, to make sure Treasury's frameworks are consistent with Mollie’s wider risk appetite and governance.

What you'll bring

  • Around 5+ years of experience in Treasury, ALM or balance sheet risk management, ideally within a bank, though experience in a fintech, PSP or consultancy building similar frameworks is also relevant.

  • Solid working knowledge of liquidity risk (LCR/NSFR, ILAAP) and/or interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB/CSRBB). You don't need to be deep in both, but you understand how they connect to the balance sheet as a whole.

  • Comfort building models and frameworks from a blank page. You're not looking for a well-worn playbook, you're excited to write the first one.

  • Strong quantitative and Excel/financial modelling skills, with the discipline to document your logic clearly enough that someone else, including a regulator, can follow it.

  • The ability to explain complex balance sheet risk topics clearly to non-specialists, and the confidence to defend your recommendations to senior stakeholders.

  • Genuine curiosity about how AI can speed up the parts of this work that don't need a human, so more of your time goes toward judgment and design.

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy.

If you're excited by the idea of building a bank's Treasury function from scratch, for Mollie and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV (in English) using the form below.

Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie is really like.

AI at Mollie

We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every role, every day.

AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance and banking with us.

title: Director of Accounting & Controlling
description:
Imagine this. You are building the accounting and controlling backbone behind a fast-growing aerospace and defence company operating across multiple countries, manufacturing sites, and legal entities. As Director of Accounting & Controlling, you will own the integrity of our group financial reporting, set the standard for IFRS and local GAAP compliance, and make sure our numbers are accurate, controlled, scalable, and audit-ready.

Reporting directly to the CFO, you will be the group's senior technical accounting authority and a key finance leader across the organization. This is not a role for someone who wants to manage accounting from a distance. You will set the agenda, challenge existing processes, solve complex accounting issues, and drive execution across a distributed international finance organization.

At Destinus, we are revolutionizing the defense industry with cutting-edge Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our innovative technologies are designed to meet the unique demands of modern defense operations, delivering unparalleled speed, precision, and cost effectiveness. Destinus partners with government agencies and defense organizations worldwide to provide advanced solutions for mission-critical operations, enabling a new era of efficiency and technological superiority. Join us in shaping the future of defense with groundbreaking aerospace innovations.

What You'll Do

  • Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual group close across all consolidated entities, ensuring accurate, complete, and timely financial reporting
  • Own the group close calendar and drive execution across Accounting, Controlling, FP&A, Tax, Treasury, and regional finance teams
  • Act as the senior escalation point for complex accounting and close issues, driving them to resolution without compromising reporting quality or timelines
  • Coordinate consolidation adjustments, intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, and other group-level accounting activities
  • Own and continuously strengthen internal accounting controls, policies, and their consistent application across the group
  • Drive improvements to our ERP and finance systems landscape, including Microsoft Dynamics environments, IFRS and local GAAP configurations, regional VAT setups, transfer pricing, intercompany eliminations, and consolidation processes
  • Own group-wide cost accounting standards and methodologies across manufacturing entities, including standard and actual costing, absorption, WIP, and variance analysis
  • Lead the Operations Finance function through the Operations Finance Lead and ensure disciplined capture and reporting of manufacturing costs including labor, overhead, scrap, absorption, and WIP
  • Own the variance bridge process and ensure significant deviations are understood, explained, and assigned to the right accountable teams across Manufacturing, Program Management, Procurement, and Finance
  • Connect Cost Accounting, Operations, Manufacturing, and Program Management so operational drivers such as volume, yield, labor mix, and capacity utilization are reflected in forecasts and budgets
  • Partner closely with FP&A to ensure accounting actuals, forecasts, and budgets remain methodologically aligned as the business scales
  • Own accounting judgments related to inventory, WIP, and program cost capitalization under IAS 2
  • Govern the group chart of accounts and ensure it remains consistent, scalable, and aligned with consolidation and management reporting requirements
  • Own balance sheet quality across the group, establishing clear standards for account ownership, reconciliations, substantiation, aging, suspense accounts, clearing accounts, and provisions
  • Partner with FP&A and Treasury on working capital, provisions, capex accounting, and other balance sheet forecasting inputs
  • Oversee AP and AR processes across the group, strengthening controls, segregation of duties, cash conversion, and sub-ledger reconciliation
  • Drive DSO and DPO discipline and establish robust policies around credit control, payment terms, and dispute resolution
  • Act as the primary management counterpart for external auditors across group and statutory audits
  • Own audit timelines, PBC processes, technical accounting documentation, and the timely resolution of audit findings
  • Ensure statutory financial statements are accurate and filed on time across jurisdictions in coordination with local teams and external advisors
  • Support lender and investor diligence with accurate, audit-ready financial schedules and clear technical accounting narratives
  • Standardize accounting processes and controls across entities and eliminate unnecessary manual workarounds as the organization grows
  • Partner with IT and ERP teams to build scalable accounting, costing, consolidation, and reporting structures within systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365
  • Own group accounting policies, procedures, and SOPs, creating a consistent framework for control, onboarding, and training
  • Build and develop a high-performing accounting and controlling organization across multiple European jurisdictions, setting clear expectations and creating accountability across direct and indirect teams
  • Mentor Controllers and Accounting Managers across the group and act as the technical escalation point when complex accounting decisions need to be made

Requirements

What You'll Need

  • 10+ years of progressive Accounting, Controlling, or Finance experience, including substantial responsibility within a multi-entity, multi-currency European environment
  • Public company experience is required
  • Deep technical knowledge of IFRS and strong familiarity with local GAAP requirements across European jurisdictions
  • Demonstrated experience owning group accounting policies and making complex technical accounting judgments
  • Proven experience leading group close and consolidation processes at significant scale, ideally within environments exceeding EUR 1 billion in revenue
  • Strong manufacturing cost accounting experience, including standard and actual costing, variance analysis, absorption, inventory, and WIP
  • Experience working closely with Manufacturing and Operations teams, with the ability to connect operational performance with financial outcomes
  • Strong ERP experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, Oracle, or an equivalent large-scale platform, including exposure to chart-of-accounts design, costing structures, consolidation, and finance transformation
  • Experience leading geographically distributed finance teams and developing senior accounting and controlling professionals
  • Excellent English communication skills, with additional European languages considered an advantage
  • Experience within aerospace, defence, industrial manufacturing, or another regulated and program-driven environment is strongly preferred
  • Experience with statutory reporting requirements across multiple European jurisdictions is a strong advantage
  • Familiarity with program-based revenue recognition, government or institutional customers, and complex manufacturing environments is an advantage.

Who You Are

You combine technical accounting depth with the drive to get things done. You care about clean numbers, strong controls, and clear ownership, but you also understand that Finance needs to move at the speed of the business.

You are comfortable being the person people turn to when the accounting answer is not obvious. You challenge assumptions, translate complex IFRS topics into practical decisions, and know when to go deep and when to move quickly.

You think beyond the next close. You build processes, systems, and teams that can support a company as it grows across countries, manufacturing sites, and increasingly complex operations. You work naturally across Accounting, FP&A, Treasury, Tax, Manufacturing, Operations, and leadership, and you are persistent about getting decisions and open issues to closure.

Most importantly, you build capability around you. You develop strong teams, create accountability, and make sure critical accounting knowledge is embedded across the organization rather than concentrated in one person.

As a Senior AI Engineer, you build the intelligence behind that shift: LLM agents that understand what a brand looks like, retrieval systems that ground every generation in real brand knowledge, and automated pipelines that turn messy client material into structure machines can work with.

 

The hard problem in generative AI is no longer generation. It's control, consistency, and trust — making unpredictable models behave reliably for brands that care deeply about how they show up in the world. That's the problem you'll own.

What You'll Work On 

  • LLM agents - designing focused, reliable agents that translate brand intent into precise creative direction

  • Prompt engineering & orchestration - crafting, testing, and versioning the prompts that steer agents and generation, and building the system that assembles them - prompting as an engineering discipline, not trial and error

  • Retrieval & RAG - grounding generation in each brand's rules, assets, and visual language, with strict isolation between clients

  • Evaluation & experimentation - systematic measurement (RAGAS or similar), A/B testing, and regression gates, so quality is proven rather than assumed

  • Data extraction & OCR - pipelines that pull structure out of documents, decks, scans, and imagery; OCR and vision models for reading, understanding, and tagging whatever a client hands us

  • Automation - end-to-end pipelines that run without babysitting: classify, extract, propose, verify - humans review outcomes instead of doing the work by hand

  • Model training - fine-tuning LLMs and neural networks where prompting hits its ceiling, running models locally or hosted depending on what the job needs

  • Client-facing impact - your pipelines run against real client data and real production volume, and the results are visible in everything that ships


Who You Are

You build systems that make AI predictable, controllable, and production-ready — especially in visual domains.

You Have:

  • Strong experience with LLM-based systems in production (agents, RAG, orchestration)

  • Hands-on work with evaluation frameworks and structured experimentation — quality you can prove, not claim

  • Solid programming skills across TypeScript and Python, with experience shipping working systems

  • Experience training or fine-tuning models and managing their lifecycle

  • Exposure to generative image pipelines and what it takes to make their output usable (not theoretical interest — actual contact)

You Think:

  • In systems, not prompts — how components interact, fail, and scale

  • In constraints — how to guide models toward predictable outputs

  • In data — extraction, classification, and structure as the foundation everything else stands on

  • Pragmatically — you ship working solutions and refine based on results

Your Skills Are:

  • Translating abstract creative direction into structured AI workflows

  • Turning messy, unstructured material into clean, reliable data pipelines

  • Debugging LLM and retrieval behavior across multiple layers of a pipeline

  • Communicating across engineering and creative teams

Why Join Grip?

The Platform Position.
Grip is infrastructure for enterprise creative production—powering global brands to generate content at scale with control and consistency.

The Market Timing.
AI-generated content is moving from experimentation to production. The challenge is no longer generation—it’s control, reliability, and scale.

The Technical Moat.
You’ll work with ComfyUI-based workflows, multi-tenant architecture, and a stack spanning TypeScript, Python, Elixir, and C#—built for production, not demos.

The Work.
You will define how AI is actually used in real-world creative systems—turning unpredictable models into dependable pipelines.

Set up, configure, and troubleshoot custom ComfyUI workflows for image generation, image editing, inpainting, outpainting, upscaling, relighting, variation generation, and controlled composition.

You will connect models, nodes, prompts, masks, ControlNet inputs, LoRAs, reference images, and post-processing steps into repeatable workflows. The goal is not a one-off good image. The goal is a workflow that can produce consistent, usable outputs across many assets.

Apply AI to Production Content Problems

Use generative AI techniques against real production needs: adjusting apparel/footwear/accessories/equipment imagery, refining fashion/sportswear product shots, extending scenes, improving model consistency, generating controlled variations, or supporting creative teams with rapid image exploration.

You should understand that production images are judged on details: skin texture, garment fit, fabric behavior, seams, logos, lighting direction, pose plausibility, background continuity, and whether the image still feels brand-correct after generation.

You will test new models, identify where they improve or break the pipeline, and help the team decide when a tool is production-ready. You do not need every new release to be perfect. You need to know how to evaluate it, isolate failure modes, and translate it into a usable workflow.

You will work with CGI artists, creative technologists, production leads, and platform teams to connect creative intent with operational execution. Who You Are

You live at the intersection of image-making and systems-building. You care about the final image, but you also care about the workflow that created it.

 

You Have

A strong working knowledge of current image-generation methods: diffusion models, LoRAs, ControlNet, inpainting, outpainting, image-to-image workflows, upscaling, masking, reference-based generation, and controlled variation.

Experience producing or refining commercial-quality imagery. Fashion, sportswear, product, talent, ecommerce, campaign adaptation, or CGI production experience is a strong plus.

 

You Think

Systems-first. A good prompt is useful; a repeatable workflow is better.

Automation-first. Manual fixes are acceptable only when they teach the pipeline what to solve next.

Visually. You can tell when an image fails because of lighting, anatomy, garment behavior, material response, identity drift, composition, or post-processing artifacts.
